category_l2: Encoded path separator (%2F/%2f/%5C/%5c) routing/decoding mismatch: the router matches the raw encoded path, while StaticDirectoryHandler and middleware.Static unescape before resolving files, so a request can evade route/group middleware and read a file under the configured static root. The first fix (4.15.3/5.2.0) rejected only encoded separators and was partial; 4.15.4/5.2.1 disable static path unescaping by default.

discrepancies.detail: The first fix rejected only encoded separators (%2F/%2f/%5C/%5c). Other percent-encoded paths still reached the unescape, so /%61dmin/secret.txt and /public/%2E%2E/admin/secret.txt still returned the protected file at v4.15.3 (reproduced: 200 + TOP-SECRET, go test exit=1) and at v4.15.4 they return 404 (exit=0). The complete fix (v4.15.4 / d16a4ecf, v5.2.1 / 78c3d95) removes internal/pathutil and makes Static/StaticFS and the Static middleware stop unescaping by default; unescaping is opt-in through Echo.EnablePathUnescapingStaticFiles / StaticConfig.EnablePathUnescaping. The v4.15.4 CHANGELOG calls this a breaking change. The v4.15.4 middleware test keeps an explicit 'nok, encoded slash bypasses ACL when EnablePathUnescaping=true' case, so the opted-in configuration remains vulnerable by design.

category_l2: Reverse-proxy response handling: finalizeResponse returns early for HTTP 101 Switching Protocols before removeConnectionHeaders and the hopHeaders deletion loop, and handleUpgradeResponse copies the whole upstream header map, so hop-by-hop headers (Alt-Svc, Keep-Alive, Proxy-Authenticate, Transfer-Encoding, Trailer, Connection-named headers) reach the client on WebSocket upgrades while being stripped on ordinary responses.

additional_verified_affected.evidence: The identical imports-key code injection reproduces on the 3.10.1 tag blob: lodash.js line 10727 assigns options.imports with assignWith(baseAssign({}, ...)) and line 10810 passes the keys to Function(importsKeys, ...), with no reForbiddenIdentifierChars check anywhere in 3.x. comma-pad and undefined-value payloads both set the marker. CVE-2021-23337's own OSV range starts at introduced 0, consistent with 3.x being affected.

category_l2: Code injection through template compilation: `_.template` merges the caller-supplied `options.imports` with `assignInWith` (so inherited enumerable keys are copied), never validates the merged key names, and passes them as parameter names to `Function(importsKeys, ...)`. Key names containing commas, parentheses, braces, brackets, slashes or whitespace break out of the parameter list and execute at template call time. Only the separate `variable` option was validated, a gap left by the CVE-2021-23337 fix.
discrepancies: Patched-version disagreement: CVE.org and the GitHub advisory say 4.18.1; OSV and NVD's CPE range say 4.18.0. Source inspection shows the validation already present in 4.18.0. The dossier records 4.18.1 and states the 4.18.0 caveat.

The advisory's only fix reference, 3469357c (2021-02-17), is the CVE-2021-23337 `variable`-option fix and is an ancestor of 4.17.21, 4.17.23, 4.18.0 and 4.18.1. A check that treats any referenced fix commit as an ancestor as 'not affected' would wrongly clear this snapshot. The real fix, 879aaa93, is identified by its message (it names both this CVE and the GHSA), its diff, and its ancestry: absent at 4.17.23, present at 4.18.0/4.18.1.
Severity disagreement: NVD primary 9.8 CRITICAL (AC:L) versus CNA/GitHub/OSV 8.1 HIGH (AC:H). Same impact metrics, different attack complexity.

lodash 4.17.22 was never published to npm (registry time and versions jump 4.17.21 to 4.17.23), yet every advisory range includes it. Ranges over this ecosystem must not be read as 'every version in between exists'.

The published npm tarball of 4.17.23 ships a lodash.js (sha256 71b4b7f5) that differs from the git tag blob (sha256 2dc5f1b8) yet contains the same vulnerable construct at the same lines and reproduces. The snapshot is the git tag; the npm build is independent corroboration, not the snapshot content.

The plain release tag 4.17.23 and the channel tag 4.17.23-npm are different commits (dec55b7a, 159 files vs 835a537f, 1054 built files). The evaluation target is the plain source tag; the channel tag was considered and rejected as a distribution artifact (see the abandoned 4.17.22-npm recon).

npm marks lodash@4.18.0 deprecated with the message 'Bad release. Please use lodash@4.17.21 instead.' (lodash-es, lodash-amd and lodash.template 4.18.0 are likewise deprecated). That explains why CVE.org and the GitHub advisory recommend 4.18.1 while OSV and NVD's CPE boundary stop at 4.18.0. The reason for the deprecation is not documented in the repository history; only the npm deprecation string is public evidence.

The published lower bound >=4.0.0 is incomplete: the same imports-key injection reproduces on lodash 3.10.1, which has the assignWith/Function sink at 10727/10810 and no reForbiddenIdentifierChars check (see affected_packages[0].range_completeness). The upper bound is unaffected. The dataset keeps the authoritative published range instead of inventing a wider one, and does not claim to know the lowest affected version.

category_l2: Uncontrolled recursion in the single-document YAML parser: SingleDocParser::HandleFlowSequence consumes a '[' token, calls HandleNode, and HandleNode dispatches back into HandleFlowSequence for the next '['. There is no depth counter anywhere in the parser at 0.6.2, so a document of n opening brackets creates O(n) nested C++ stack frames and the process crashes with SIGSEGV before any syntax error is reported. The same cycle exists for flow maps ('{'), compact maps and the scanner's token queue; the 0.7.0 fix bounds it with a DepthGuard at HandleNode.
discrepancies: Fixed-version disagreement between ecosystems: Debian's tracker and OSV record say fixed_version 0.6.3-1, while upstream vanilla 0.6.3 still crashes and the fix commit 4edff1f is not an ancestor of 0.6.3. Debian 0.6.3-1 is a patched package that backports PR 807 (its changelog names CVE-2019-6285 and the patch says it 'cherry-picks the (so-far-unmerged) upstream pull request'). The first upstream release containing the fix is 0.7.0, and that is what the dossier records as the fixed release.

Two sibling CVEs (CVE-2018-20573 Scanner::EnsureTokensInQueue, CVE-2018-20574 HandleFlowMap) are labelled CWE-119 by NVD while CVE-2019-6285 and CVE-2019-6292 are labelled CWE-674. All four are the same stack-exhaustion defect fixed by the same commit; CWE-119 is a misclassification of uncontrolled recursion as a buffer issue.

The CVE.org CNA container ships a placeholder affected object: vendor, product and version are all 'n/a' and problemTypes is 'n/a', so the record itself states no version, CVSS or CWE. Its only reference is issue 660; the CVE Program ADP container adds a 2024 seclists fulldisclosure post. The exact 0.6.2 range comes from NVD's CPE and OSV's GIT range, not from the CVE record itself.

The affected range is not exhaustive: vanilla 0.6.3 is also affected although the published Debian range ends at 0.6.3-1, and older releases with the same parser (0.6.0, 0.6.1, and 0.5.x for the 2017 CVE) were not bisected. The published range and CPE name only 0.6.2.

The fix merged upstream with DepthGuard<2000> but the 0.7.0 release carries DepthGuard<500>, lowered by commit c2793a3 (2020-07-23, 'Fix runtime exceptions in Visual Studio environment. (#926)'). The recorded fixed release therefore rejects nesting at depth 500, not 2000.

CVE-2019-6292 is not covered by a named regression test in the fix commit, although it shares the same root cause and issue family (issue 657 lists HandleCompactMap, HandleMap, HandleFlowSequence, HandleSequence and HandleNode). The fix is family-wide because every path goes through HandleNode.

category_l2: Uncaught error in the microservice server: ServerTCP#handleMessage and ServerRMQ#handleMessage convert a client-controlled non-string message pattern with JSON.stringify to derive the handler lookup key. JSON.parse accepts nesting that JSON.stringify cannot re-serialise, so a deeply nested pattern parses on arrival and then throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. The listener's promise is not caught, the RangeError becomes an unhandled rejection, and Node.js exits under its default --unhandled-rejections=throw. The fix guards the stringification with getPatternAsString and routes handleMessage rejections to handleError.
discrepancies: The fix references do not agree with release containment. GHSA, OSV, NVD and CVE.org all name aa97b514 (the PR head) as a fix commit, but that commit is an ancestor of no tag; the PR was squash-merged as e93c8e12b (in v12.0.2+) and the 11.x line received the dedicated backport e9dcd4c7 (in v11.2.4+). The dossier records all three with their measured ancestry so no reader mistakes aa97b514 for the release-bearing fix.

The publication timestamps differ by surface: CVE.org and OSV say 2026-09-28T21:21:25Z, NVD says 2026-09-28T22:17:32Z, and the GHSA API says 2026-09-29T23:54:44Z. Both 11.2.4 and 12.0.2 are inside the range of the separate advisory GHSA-96h4-vgxj-gvm2, fixed in 11.2.5 / 12.0.3. category_l2: JoinHandle::abort() performs the task shutdown on the calling thread. category_l2: artifactV4Routes.buildSignature feeds endpoint, expires, artifactName, taskID and artifactID into the HMAC as raw concatenated bytes. Because artifactName has no delimiter or length prefix before the decimal taskID/artifactID, distinct tuples can serialize to the same byte stream (e.g. artifactName 'artifact-795-153' with taskID 48 versus artifactName 'artifact-795-1' with taskID 53, artifactID '48<id>'): the signature verifies for a tuple the signer never approved. The UploadArtifact and DownloadArtifact routes are unauthenticated and guarded only by ArtifactV4Contexter; after verification verifySignature loads the task by the URL's taskID and the handlers look the artifact up by name, so a forged tuple can read another task's/repository's artifact or write into another task's upload staging state.

category_l2: Urlizer.trim_punctuation() trims wrapping punctuation in a fixpoint loop. For every candidate opening/closing pair it calls middle.count(closing) and middle.count(opening) on the whole word, and each iteration only removes one bracket per side, so a word made of tens of thousands of brackets is rescanned once per bracket. Because handle_word() calls trim_punctuation() for any word containing '.', '@' or ':', passing such text through the urlize/urlizetrunc template filters consumes quadratic CPU and memory (CWE-130 improper handling of length parameter inconsistency; CWE-770 allocation without limits).

category_l2: The floatformat template filter converts its input with Decimal(str(text)) and then computes `int(d) - d`. Decimal keeps a scientific-notation value as a short coefficient plus an exponent, so parsing is cheap, but int(d) materialises every digit implied by the exponent. A string such as '1e10000000000000000' therefore asks for an astronomically large integer and exhausts memory. The 4.2.15 fix inspects Decimal.as_tuple() first and returns the input unchanged when len(digits)+abs(exponent) > 200 (CWE-400 uncontrolled resource consumption).

category_l2: get_supported_language_variant() builds possible_lang_codes from the caller string by appending one slice per hyphen (rfind loop), then probes each candidate with code.lower() against the supported-language map. category_l2: Urlizer.handle_word matches simple_url_re/simple_url_2_re against the whole untruncated word and, on a match, sends every character through smart_urlquote() (urlsplit, punycode on the netloc, unquote/quote on the path) with no length cap; is_email_simple() has no bound on the domain part, so a multi-megabyte unicode domain also reaches punycode(). category_l2: strip_tags() (django/utils/html.py) re-runs _strip_once() in a while loop until the number of '<' characters stops changing, with no bound on the number of iterations. _strip_once() feeds the whole remaining string to MLStripper(HTMLParser) and removes exactly one level of nesting per pass, so an input of the form '<'*d + 'a>'*d is scanned d times: O(d * len(value)). At 4.2.13 a 24,000-character input (d=8000) takes 25.78 s; depth 500 already costs 0.0996 s and each doubling of d multiplies the cost by about four. The striptags template filter exposes the same path to template content. 4.2.17 adds MAX_STRIP_TAGS_DEPTH = 50 and raises SuspiciousOperation once the loop reaches the cap, so the same inputs fail in 0.018-0.333 s (CWE-770 allocation of resources without limits or throttling).

category_l2: HasKeyLookup.as_oracle() (django/db/models/fields/json.py) composes the Oracle SQL in two steps: HasKeyLookup.as_sql() builds 'JSON_EXISTS(<lhs>, %s)' from the lhs SQL and returns the lhs bind params together with the JSON paths, and as_oracle() then applies `sql % tuple(params)` to that composed string and returns an empty param list. Every lhs parameter is therefore pasted into the SQL text instead of being sent as a bind variable, so when application code passes untrusted data as the lhs of a direct HasKey(lhs, rhs) query, that data becomes SQL syntax. At 4.2.13 an lhs of "'x') OR 1=1 --" compiles to JSON_EXISTS('x') OR 1=1 --, '$."a"') with no params; a JSON object lhs is inlined the same way. The 4.2.17 fix splits the composition into _as_sql_parts()/_combine_sql_parts() and gives as_oracle() a template that inlines only the JSON path while returning the lhs params, so the same lhs compiles to JSON_EXISTS(%s, '$."a"') with the value bound. The has_key lookup through __ is unaffected on both releases (CWE-89).

category_l2: PasswordResetForm.send_mail() (django/contrib/auth/forms.py) calls email_message.send() without any exception handling. When the configured mail backend raises, the exception escapes PasswordResetForm.save() and the PasswordResetView returns a server error. save() only reaches send_mail() for the users get_users() returns, i.e. addresses that exist, are active and have a usable password; nonexistent addresses produce no send and no error. An attacker who submits addresses and observes the outcome can therefore tell which addresses have accounts (CWE-203/CWE-204), provided email sending is consistently failing. The 4.2.16 fix wraps send() in try/except and logs the failure on the django.contrib.auth logger, so both cases produce the same outcome (CWE-203).

category_l2: Q.__init__ (django/db/models/query_utils.py 48-53) accepts an arbitrary _connector and forwards it to tree.Node; WhereNode.as_sql (django/db/models/sql/where.py 171-172) joins the child SQL with ' %s ' % self.connector, so the string is interpolated straight into the query. category_l2: QuerySet.annotate(**kwargs) and QuerySet.alias(**kwargs) dispatch a FilteredRelation value to Query.add_filtered_relation() (django/db/models/sql/query.py 1622-1651 at 4.2.13), which stores the dictionary key as filtered_relation.alias without calling the existing Query.check_alias(). The alias later becomes a join table alias and Join.as_sql (django/db/models/sql/datastructures.py 118-127) interpolates it raw: `alias_str = " %s" % self.table_alias`, so a key containing a double quote, whitespace and an SQL comment escapes the join and comments out the generated ON/WHERE clauses. With the two params still binding into placeholders kept inside the injected text, the join can be made unconditional (filter bypass) or a condition on an arbitrary subquery (boolean oracle over author.secret). 4.2.24 adds self.check_alias(alias) to add_filtered_relation, and every crafted alias then raises ValueError before SQL is built while benign aliases are unchanged.

category_l2: django.utils.archive.extract() (used by startapp --template and startproject --template) resolves each archive member with BaseArchive.target_filename() (django/utils/archive.py 144-149 at 4.2.13): it computes the absolute path under the target directory and accepts it when `filename.startswith(target_path)`. String prefix is weaker than path containment, so an archive member such as '../target-evil/pwned.txt' — or an absolute '<target>abc/evil.txt' as in the upstream regression test — resolves to a sibling directory whose name starts with the target path and is written outside it. Members that escape without sharing the prefix (plain '../outside.txt') were already rejected. 4.2.25 compares os.path.commonpath([target_path, filename]) with target_path instead (and maps the different-drive ValueError on Windows to the same SuspiciousOperation), so the sibling path is rejected while benign members extract unchanged.

category_l2: django.utils.log.log_response() (django/utils/log.py 241-249 at 4.2.13) forwards the caller's positional formatting arguments to the logger unchanged. django.core.handlers.base.BaseHandler.get_response() (django/core/handlers/base.py 143-149) calls it for every 4xx/5xx response with ('%s: %s', response.reason_phrase, request.path), and request.path is attacker-controlled (the WSGI server percent-decodes PATH_INFO). A URL containing %0A or %1B therefore reaches the log record - and any file or terminal formatter - as a real newline or ANSI escape: a single request can forge an extra log line, or recolor/relabel terminal output. 4.2.22 encodes every string argument with `unicode_escape` before logging (so %0A becomes the two characters \n); the 4.2.23 follow-up migrates the remaining django.views.generic.base logging to log_response().

category_l2: django.core.serializers.xml_serializer.getInnerText() (django/core/serializers/xml_serializer.py 393-407 at 4.2.13) recurses over element children and does `inner_text.extend(getInnerText(child))`. getInnerText() returns a string, so extend() appends one list element per character of the child's text; every recursion level therefore copies the entire leaf text again, and the final join repeats it once more. The documented XML deserializer path - serializers.deserialize('xml', data) -> Deserializer.__next__ -> expandNode -> _handle_object - calls getInnerText(field_node) for each field value, so a document with a deeply nested <field> and a long leaf makes deserialization cost O(depth x leaf) for linear input. 4.2.27 replaces the recursion with getInnerTextList() (collect once, join once) and wraps expandNode() in fast_cache_clearing(), a workaround for minidom's _in_document full-tree check.

category_l2: django.utils.text.wrap() (django/utils/text.py 88-117 at 4.2.13) wraps each input line with a hand-written loop: every iteration yields about `width` characters and then rebinds `line = line[space:]`, copying the entire remaining string. For n characters of many short words the loop runs about n/width times, so total copying is O(n^2/width) for O(n) input. The documented template filter wordwrap (django/template/defaultfilters.py 398-400) calls wrap(value, int(arg)) directly, so a template that applies `|wordwrap` to a long attacker-influenced string is the exposed path. 4.2.20 replaces the loop with textwrap.TextWrapper(width, break_long_words=False, break_on_hyphens=False) and joins the wrapped lines once.

category_l2: ASGIRequest.__init__ (django/core/handlers/asgi.py 83-97 at 4.2.13) folds every (name, value) pair from the ASGI scope into META with `if corrected_name in self.META: value = self.META[corrected_name] + "," + value` and then writes it back. Each duplicate of one header therefore copies the whole accumulated value twice (once for the ',' join, once for the value append), so m duplicates of a v-byte header copy about (v+1)*m^2 bytes and do m dict writes for O(m*v) attacker input. A remote attacker controls the header list through the ASGI server (HTTP/2 repeats headers cheaply), and the upstream regression test uses 200,000 duplicates. 4.2.28 groups values in a collections.defaultdict(list) and joins each name once with self.META.update(), making the merge linear.

category_l2: Truncator._truncate_html (django/utils/text.py 215-300 at 4.2.13) walks the input with re_chars/re_words and keeps the open tags in a plain list. For every end tag it calls `open_tags.index(tagname)` (line 276) and, on a hit, rebuilds the list with `open_tags = open_tags[i + 1 :]` (line 282). An input made of start tags followed by many unmatched end tags never hits that branch, so each of the m end tags scans all m open tags and the parse costs O(m^2) Python-level comparisons - about 3.1 s for 112 KB (n=16,000) in the measured ladder, with a ~1.9 log2 slope per doubling. Because the payload contains no text characters, `current_len` never reaches `truncate_len`, so the loop keeps parsing every tag even when the caller asks for a tiny preview (truncatechars_html:2, truncatewords_html:1). 4.2.28 replaces the scan with the LIFO check `if open_tags and open_tags[0] == tagname` and the list slice with `open_tags[1:]`, which removes the Python-level scan; the `open_tags.insert(0, tagname)` call and the per-close slice copy remain, so the backport is ~10-21x faster on this payload but is not linear on well-nested input either.

category_l2: HttpRequest.body checks DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE against the declared CONTENT_LENGTH only (django/http/request.py 331-339 at 4.2.13) and then calls self.read() (342), which drains the whole stream. On the ASGI path ASGIHandler.read_body accumulates every chunk into a SpooledTemporaryFile (asgi.py 192-211) without any size cap, and a chunked request carries no Content-Length, so `int(META.get('CONTENT_LENGTH') or 0)` is 0 and the limit never fires. 4.2.30 adds _check_data_too_big plus a seekable-stream size check (and a limit+1 read for non-seekable streams).

category_l2: In django/http/multipartparser.py, the base64 branch of the file part loop strips whitespace from the current parser chunk (stripped_chunk, 305), then aligns it to a multiple of four by calling `field_stream.read(4 - remaining)` (309) once per 1-3 bytes and appending in place (312). LazyStream.read slices the current leftover and calls unget(chunk[remaining:]) (441-465), which rebuilds `self._leftover` as bytes + leftover; with a long whitespace run after three base64 characters each 1-byte read replays the rest of the current 64 KiB chunk, so that chunk is re-copied once per whitespace byte and the in-place append grows as well, giving quadratic copying within each chunk. 4.2.30 reads self._chunk_size per iteration and joins a stripped_parts list once.

category_l2: In django/contrib/admin/options.py, ModelAdmin.changelist_view builds a changelist formset from the POSTed data when cl.list_editable and '_save' are present (2003-2012). category_l2: In django/contrib/auth/handlers/modwsgi.py, check_password() looks the user up with get_by_natural_key() and returns None immediately for a nonexistent user (19-21) or an inactive one (22-23). Only an active user reaches user.check_password() (24), which runs the default PBKDF2 hasher. A remote attacker abusing mod_wsgi authentication therefore gets a fast response for usernames that do not exist and a ~300x slower one for existing active usernames, which discloses account existence. 4.2.28 adds _get_user(), which runs UserModel().set_password("") whenever the lookup ends in None, equalising the runtime.

category_l2: FileSystemStorage._save() and FileBasedCache._createdir() changed the process-wide umask with os.umask() around os.makedirs() to force directory permissions, restoring it afterwards. In a multi-threaded server every other thread that creates a file or directory inside that window inherits the masked mode, so objects can be created with permissions the concurrent request never asked for. 4.2.29 replaces both sites with a vendored makedirs()/safe_makedirs() that creates directories recursively and applies the requested mode with os.chmod() after os.mkdir(), without touching the global umask.

category_l2: UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response() skips caching a response that sets a cookie and varies on Cookie only when the incoming request carried no cookies at all (the `not request.COOKIES` precondition, 91-98). A request that already carries any unrelated cookie - a language or theme preference, a consent flag - therefore stores the response, including its newly issued session cookie and private body, in the shared cache under a key that varies only by the Cookie header. cache_page() wraps the same CacheMiddleware through decorator_from_middleware_with_args(), so the decorator inherits the defect. 5.2.16 drops the precondition and refuses to cache whenever response.cookies and has_vary_header(response, "Cookie") hold.

category_l2: UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response() decides whether a response marked private may be cached with the case-sensitive test `"private" in response.get("Cache-Control", ())` (4.2.13 line 101). A response whose header reads `Private` or `pRiVaTe` therefore fails the test, falls through to patch_response_headers()/learn_cache_key() and is stored in the shared cache; FetchFromCacheMiddleware then serves it to other clients. cache_page() wraps the same CacheMiddleware through decorator_from_middleware_with_args(), so the decorator inherits the defect. 5.2.15 and 6.0.6 lowercase the header value and reject private, no-cache and no-store; 6.1 parses directive names into a set. The release notes state that cache_control()/patch_cache_control() were not affected because they lowercase, so only responses with manually set Cache-Control are affected.

category_l2: UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response() calls django.utils.cache.has_vary_header() to decide whether a response may be cached: the Cookie guard refuses to cache a cookie-less request's response that sets a cookie, and (since 5.0) the wildcard guard refuses Vary: *. has_vary_header() splits the Vary value on commas and lowercases the parts without stripping surrounding whitespace, so Vary: ' Cookie' or ' *' is not recognized. The response is stored under a key that also ignores the spaced header name, and FetchFromCacheMiddleware serves it to other clients. The upstream fix adds .strip(); 4.2 LTS was end-of-life and has no patched release, and its middleware has no wildcard guard at all, so the 4.2 exposure that the fix would remove is the Cookie-guard bypass.

category_l2: QuerySet.annotate()/alias() register a dictionary-expanded alias after check_alias(), which at 4.2.13 rejects quotes, whitespace, semicolons and SQL comments but not periods. When the same alias is used in FilteredRelation and then in order_by(), SQLCompiler.get_order_by() sees the period, assumes the entry came from extra(order_by=...), splits it as table.column and emits that verbatim as RawSQL in ORDER BY. The annotation lookup is bypassed, so a crafted alias chooses the table and column used for ordering. The 4.2.28 fix restricts the dotted branch to extra_order_by entries and makes add_filtered_relation() reject periods in aliases.

category_l2: Query aliases are validated by Query.check_alias() against FORBIDDEN_ALIAS_PATTERN. At 4.2.13 the pattern rejects quotes, whitespace, semicolons, hashes absent and SQL comments, but not the control-character ranges 0x00-0x1F and 0x7F-0x9F. Those keys can reach annotate(), alias(), aggregate(), extra(), values() and values_list() through dictionary expansion, are stored as column aliases and are emitted inside the SQL identifier. The 4.2.28 fix adds both control-character ranges to the pattern and updates the ValueError message; the tests sweep every code point in those ranges for annotate(), alias() and FilteredRelation.

category_l2: PostGIS raster lookups splice a band index from a RasterField lookup into the SQL template. At 4.2.13 PostGISOperator.check_raster() interpolates lookup.band_lhs/band_rhs with "%s, %s" and performs no type check, so a string supplied as the band index lands verbatim in the generated SQL fragment (the probe records '%s, 1) UNION SELECT 1 --'). GISLookup.process_band_indices() is what copies the untrusted rhs tuple element into band_rhs. The 4.2.28 fix requires both band indices to be int and raises TypeError otherwise.

category_l2: QuerySet.alias()/annotate() route a FilteredRelation alias supplied through **kwargs dictionary expansion to Query.add_filtered_relation(), which stores the attacker-chosen key as the join alias. The SQL compiler then emits that alias through SQLCompiler.quote_name_unless_alias(); because the alias is in query.alias_map it is returned unquoted. At 4.2.13 the PostgreSQL backend has no override, so a key containing $ reaches the SQL token stream verbatim (probe: JOIN "probeapp_author" crafted_alia$). 4.2.27 adds django/db/backends/postgresql/compiler.py, which rejects any alias containing $ with ValueError and is wired via DatabaseOperations.compiler_module.

category_l2: HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__ sets the Location header and then calls urlparse(str(redirect_to)) so the destination scheme can be checked. At 4.2.13 there is no upper bound on that string: a very large attacker-supplied redirect target reaches urllib.parse.urlsplit(), which NFKC-normalizes a non-ASCII netloc with unicodedata.normalize(). Python's NFKC normalization is slow on Windows, so repeated large redirects can exhaust CPU. The same path is reachable through HttpResponsePermanentRedirect and django.shortcuts.redirect(). 4.2.26 adds a 2048-character cap before urlparse, relaxed to 16384 in 4.2.27.

category_l2: GeoDjango hands WKT/WKB/hex-WKB straight to GEOS. category_l2: The Content-Disposition header regex is not anchored to the start of a line and pairs a greedy (.*) with an end-of-line lookahead, so the regexp engine restarts the scan at every offset where the literal occurs. The 1536-byte disposition cap is applied after the match and the header block is bounded only by the blank-line terminator. When one part header line contains many literal occurrences and no CRLF followed by a non-whitespace character after them (a folded continuation line starting with whitespace is enough), every occurrence pays an O(rest of line) backtracking scan, i.e. quadratic work in the header-line length. A single occurrence followed by a long value only pays one scan and stays linear. v3.1.16 anchors all three header regexes at ^ with FWS/HEADER_VALUE.

category_l2: handle_mime_head waits for the CRLFCRLF that terminates a MIME part header by scanning the shared buffer with @head_regex. When the terminator has not arrived, the buffer is appended to (read_data: io.read(@bufsize) then @sbuf.concat) and the loop returns :want_read with no cap on how many bytes may accumulate, so a part header that never terminates is buffered in memory up to the request body size. There is no amplification: memory grows with the bytes actually sent, so the bound is the server's body limit and concurrency. v3.1.17 raises 'multipart mime part header too large' once the buffer exceeds MIME_HEADER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT = 64 KiB (effectively max(64 KiB, BUFSIZE)).

category_l2: handle_fast_forward looks for the first multipart boundary by scanning the shared buffer with consume_boundary (@sbuf.scan_until(@body_regex)). When the boundary has not arrived the else branch only returns :want_read, and read_data (io.read(@bufsize) then @sbuf.concat) keeps appending, so every byte sent before the first boundary stays resident in memory. consume_boundary calls @sbuf.terminate on failure, which moves the scan pointer to the end but does not free the string. There is no amplification in retained bytes: the resident string grows with the bytes actually sent, so the bound is the server's body limit plus concurrency (peak RSS can still reach about 1.6-2x the payload because Ruby String growth copies the buffer; the round39 reviewer measured VmHWM 141,404 kB against a 25,856 kB baseline for a 64 MiB preamble). v3.1.17 raises 'multipart boundary not found within limit' once the whole buffer is larger than BOUNDARY_START_LIMIT = 16 KiB; the check runs after each read, so the first threshold hit is the first BUFSIZE multiple above 16 KiB (1,048,576 B by default, 24,576 B with BUFSIZE 8192).

category_l2: Parts without a filename take the BufferPart branch: Collector#on_mime_head allocates body = String.new (parser.rb 160) and Collector#on_mime_body appends every chunk with @mime_parts[mime_index].body << content (170). Nothing counts the retained bytes: check_part_limits (178-195) bounds only the number of open files and the number of parts, and handle_mime_body hands over the entire part body once the boundary is found (414) or the growing tail on each read (422). A single large text field is therefore materialised in process memory. There is no amplification: retained memory tracks the bytes the client actually sends, so the bound is the server's body limit plus concurrency. v3.1.17 accounts header bytes plus non-file body bytes and raises 'multipart data over retained size limit' once @retained_size exceeds BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (default 16 MiB, configurable through RACK_MULTIPART_BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT).

category_l2: Rack::Request#POST parses application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies by calling get_header(RACK_INPUT).read with no length argument (request.rb 531 at v3.1.13), which is IO#read(nil): read everything until EOF into one Ruby String, before any size check runs. The frozen QueryParser at this tag has no byte or count limits at all (query_parser.rb 30-39: initialize takes only params_class and param_depth_limit, and the file has no BYTESIZE_LIMIT / PARAMS_LIMIT / QueryLimitError), so neither the read nor the subsequent parse is bounded. Memory therefore tracks the request body size linearly, with no amplification. 3.1.18 reads at most query_parser.bytesize_limit + 2 bytes (4 MiB default via RACK_QUERY_PARSER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT) and falls back to '' when read returns nil.

category_l2: Rack::Sendfile decides whether to enable sendfile, and which redirect header to emit, from request headers rather than from configuration. At v3.1.13 variation() (sendfile.rb 148-152) falls back to env['HTTP_X_SENDFILE_TYPE'] when the middleware was constructed without a variation, so a client can turn on x-accel-redirect (or x-sendfile, which reflects the absolute path of a to_path body). When the x-accel-redirect branch runs, map_accel_path() (154-165) falls back to env['HTTP_X_ACCEL_MAPPING'] (157) whenever no application-level mapping matched, so the client controls the filesystem-to-URL substitution that ends up in the response header at 123. A proxy that re-issues x-accel-redirect internally then serves the mapped private location unless it overwrites both headers, which is why the advisory requires the proxy to always set or strip them. Fixed in 3.1.18 by removing the HTTP_X_SENDFILE_TYPE fallback entirely, gating HTTP_X_ACCEL_MAPPING behind explicit x-accel-redirect configuration with no app mappings, and anchoring the mapping regexes with \A instead of ^.

category_l2: Flask adds Vary: Cookie so shared caches key on the session cookie. At 2.3.1 the flag that gates the header (SecureCookieSession.accessed) is set only in __getitem__, get, setdefault and on_update (sessions.py 71-87); plain dict operations inherited from CallbackDict such as `key in session`, len(session) and iteration never set it, and flask.session / the template `session` both resolve to the same object, so those reads are invisible. In addition, at this tag save_session returns early on an empty session (334) before the Vary gate (347-349), so even a value read on an empty session yields no Vary. A caching proxy that does not ignore Set-Cookie responses can then serve a session-dependent response to another user. The fix moves tracking to RequestContext.session (3.1.3 ctx.py 368-375), so resolving the proxy sets accessed before any dict operation, drops the per-method overrides, stops replacing the proxy in the template context, and uses ctx._session when saving so the save itself does not count as access.

category_l2: Request.max_form_memory_size is meant to cap in-memory form data, and MultiPartParser.parse forwards it to MultipartDecoder. At 3.0.2 the only enforcement is in MultipartDecoder.receive_data (sansio/multipart.py 139-143), which compares len(buffer) + len(chunk) against the limit for a single chunk. MultiPartParser.parse reads the body in buffer_size (64 KiB) chunks (369) and, for a non-file field, appends every Data event to a list (381-382) with no cumulative accounting, then joins and decodes the whole list when the part ends (384-388). A body whose non-file field is larger than the limit but arrives in chunks smaller than it therefore passes every per-event check and is buffered without bound; a bigger buffer_size makes the same bypass trivial. The fix 50cfeebc/8760275a tracks field_size per Field (355, 374, 383-389) and raises RequestEntityTooLarge once the accumulated field passes the limit, leaving file parts to the streaming container.

category_l2: String callable resolution in address validation. validateAddress($address, $patternselect = null) falls back to static::$validator, which defaults to the string 'php', and then returns $patternselect($address) whenever is_callable() accepts the selector (src/PHPMailer.php 1309-1311 at v6.1.5). A plain string is callable exactly when a function of that name exists in the global namespace, so a function that another primitive injected — even one unrelated to mail, named 'php' — is executed for every address validated in the default configuration, and its return value becomes the validation verdict. The fix 45f3c18d requires !is_string($patternselect) at 1341 of v6.5.0, so a string always reaches the built-in switch (case 'php' -> filter_var) and only closures/arrays are called.

The OSV/GHSA 5.x range 5.0.0 -> 5.4.16 contains 5.0.11, and the OSV CVE record's GIT range introduces the 5.x line at 0c312583 (the v5.0.0 release commit), which is an ancestor of v5.0.11.

admission_checks.notes: Derived deterministically from frozen-SHA status/location fields; no network or re-research.

category_l2: serveRawFsMiddleware checks server.fs.allow/server.fs.deny on url.pathname, which WHATWG URL parsing stops at '#'. A request-target such as /@fs<root>/#/../../outside_secret.txt therefore passes the check, and the middleware then rewrites req.url from url.href, which keeps the fragment; sirv resolves the rewritten path outside the root and returns the file. The 5.4.18 fix rejects any req.url containing '#' with 400 before the fs middlewares run.

fixed_releases.notes: Not a fix for CVE-2025-31486 (first in v5.4.17) or for the earlier fs-serve CVEs: those guards are prerequisites this commit bypasses differently. The 4.x and 6.x lines are fixed in their own commits and were not built or probed here.
fixed_releases.verified_content: git_facts records first_contained_release_tag FIX_54_823675baf=v5.4.18, ancestry 823675baf in v5.4.18 = true and in v5.4.17 = false, that 823675baf's parent is the v5.4.17 release commit, and that the v5.4.18 release commit 731b77d1's parent is 823675baf. server/index.ts at v5.4.18 registers the new middleware at 857 while v5.4.17 contains no such import or registration. The collector's v5.4.18 build answers 400 with an empty body to all eight fragment rows and still serves / and /safe.txt, while the v5.4.17 build discloses the outside file and the three deny targets for the plain and ?raw fragment rows. This is the release named by OSV/NVD/GHSA for the 5.x line.

title: Vite has a server.fs.deny bypass with an invalid request-target
vulnerable_commit_basis: Tag v5.0.11 peels to b44c4930, the commit the evaluation snapshot snap_2e50b228f2432623 pins; the probe reports read packages/vite/package.json in each built worktree and record 5.0.11. category_l2: transformMiddleware's JS branch strips the `?import` marker and unwraps the /@fs prefix, then calls transformRequest with the still-relative id and no id-level serving check (the allowId option does not exist at v5.0.11). A `?/../..` segment survives into the id; resolution normalizes it to a path outside server.fs.allow (or onto a path on server.fs.deny), and asset.ts's raw branch reads cleanUrl(id) and returns it as `export default "<contents>"`. v5.4.16 added a guard, but it runs on the request URL before normalization, and cleanUrl truncates at the first `?`, so `/@fs<root>/?/../../<file>` is judged as the in-root `/@fs<root>/`. v5.4.17 fixes this by passing allowId into transformRequest and testing the resolved id in loadAndTransform. The advisory's `.svg` clause is a separate 6.0+ assetsInlineLimit path and does not reproduce on 5.x.

fixed_releases.notes: Not a fix for CVE-2025-32395: the '#' request-target rows still disclose at v5.4.17 (round58's packet records that) and are only closed by 823675baf in v5.4.18. The probe matrices for the two releases are identical on this round's rows, which is consistent with the two fixes being independent.
fixed_releases.verified_content: git_facts records 84b2b46ed's parent as the v5.4.16 release commit 712cb71a, the v5.4.17 release commit 0a2518a9's parent as 84b2b46ed, 84b2b46ed an ancestor of v5.4.17 and not of v5.4.16. static.ts is byte-identical between v5.4.16 and v5.4.17 (sha256 5a9de0ad...), so the fix is transform-side: transform.ts 53-68 adds svgRE and deniedServingAccessForTransform, 195-200 calls it, 243-248 passes allowId into transformRequest, and transformRequest.ts 247-253 re-checks the resolved id and throws ERR_DENIED_ID. The collector's v5.4.17 build answers 403 to the five ?import& rows that disclose at v5.0.11 and v5.4.16, and the 403 body names the normalised outside path. This is the release OSV names as the 5.x GIT fixed event.

title: Vite allows server.fs.deny to be bypassed with .svg or relative paths
vulnerable_commit_basis: Tag v5.0.11 peels to b44c4930, the commit the evaluation snapshot snap_2e50b228f2432623 pins; the probe reports read packages/vite/package.json in each built worktree and record 5.0.11. The OSV GHSA 5.x range 5.0.0 -> 5.4.17 contains 5.0.11, and the OSV CVE GIT range opens the 5.x line at 0c312583 (the v5.0.0 release commit), which is an ancestor of v5.0.11.

category_l2: serveStaticMiddleware returns next() for any request whose cleanUrl ends in .html, so .html requests never reach its ensureServingAccess check (static.ts 112-119 at v5.0.11). htmlFallbackMiddleware then joins root with the decoded pathname, tests only existsSync and rewrites req.url (htmlFallback.ts 37-44), and indexHtmlMiddleware repeats the join and calls fsp.readFile + send with no server.fs allow or deny test (indexHtml.ts 422-440). A URL such as /../../../../tmp/secret.html is therefore resolved outside the root and served, and a root .html file listed in server.fs.deny is served anyway. The advisory adds that the preview server served HTML files not under the output directory. The fix 482000f57 (v5.4.20) resolves the path, calls checkLoadingAccess in dev (403 on denied) and isParentDirectory(root, filePath) in preview. v5.4.19 still has the unguarded join in indexHtml.ts even though its static.ts already carries checkLoadingAccess.

fixed_releases.notes: The 5.4.20 tag also contains the separate CVE-2025-58751 fix (sirv 3.0.2 port 4f1c35bcb). That commit touches no indexHtml.ts line, so this packet's boundary is attributable to 482000f57.

title: Vite's `server.fs` settings were not applied to HTML files
vulnerable_commit_basis: Tag v5.0.11 peels to b44c4930, the commit the evaluation snapshot snap_2e50b228f2432623 pins (git_facts). The probe reads packages/vite/package.json in the built worktree and records version 5.0.11. The OSV SEMVER range 0 -> 5.4.20 contains 5.0.11 and NVD's CPE configuration versionEndExcluding 5.4.20 does too.

admission_checks.notes: Derived deterministically from frozen-SHA status/location fields; no network or re-research.

category_l2: The advisory groups three causes that all violate the dev server's origin boundary. [2], the one this dossier locates: the HMR WebSocket listener in ws.ts (126-136 at v5.0.11) accepts an upgrade for any Origin - it compares only sec-websocket-protocol and req.url, never req.headers.origin, and there is no token - so a page on another origin can open the HMR channel and read the messages the server pushes (file paths, error source snippets, plugin messages). [1] server/index.ts 727-730 mounts cors() whenever server.cors is not literally false, so the default is Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and any site can fetch and read dev-server modules. [3] nothing in the chain inspects the Host header, so DNS rebinding can bypass the same-origin policy outright. v5.4.12 closes all three with dfea38f1f, b71a5c89a and 9da4abc8d.

title: Websites were able to send any requests to the vite development server and read the response
vulnerable_commit_basis: Tag v5.0.11 peels to b44c4930 (git_facts), the commit the evaluation snapshot snap_2e50b228f2432623 pins; packages/vite/package.json in the built worktree reads version 5.0.11. category_l2: fetch() parses the integrity option with a regular expression that only recognises a hash token when at least one base64-ish character follows the algorithm. A value such as 'sha256-ä', 'sha256-!' or 'sha256-' does not parse, the parser skips it, and the resulting empty metadata set is accepted by the unchanged empty-set rule in bytesMatch. The body is then delivered even though no declared hash matched it. The fix keeps the algorithm token when the hash is absent so the comparison fails, which in practice closes the request through a TypeError. 5.28.4 fixes the 5.x line and 6.11.1 fixes the 6.x line; the two commits are separate backports with different patch-ids.

fixed_releases.notes: The release commit is the fix commit's direct child, so the release boundary is attributable to 2b39440b alone.

The probe loads the v5.28.4 checkout: package 5.28.4, zero malformed/mixed values resolve with the tampered body.

category_l2: The Request constructor's blob-like body branch appends `content-type: ${body.type}` to the request head without calling isValidHeaderValue. A hand-rolled blob-like object whose `.type` contains CRLF therefore injects arbitrary header lines, and with a blank line plus a request line it also places a second request on the wire. The ordinary explicit-header path validates, and native Blob normalises invalid types to the empty string, so the gap is specific to the unvalidated blob branch. Fixed by validating `${body.type}` in the 6.x/7.x/8.x dispatchers; the 5.x line has no fix.

title: Vite dev server reads .map files outside the project root through the optimized-deps sourcemap branch
vulnerable_commit_basis: Tag v5.0.11 is a lightweight tag on b44c4930 (git_facts), the commit the evaluation snapshot pins; the built worktree reports package version 5.0.11. The OSV SEMVER range introduced 0 -> fixed 6.4.2 contains 5.0.11, and this round's probe shows the snapshot build returning the outside file with its marker. NVD's CPE match starts at 6.0.0 and would exclude 5.0.11; that disagreement is recorded below and the OSV bound is used because the measurement, not the metadata, decides.

admission_checks.notes: Derived deterministically from frozen-SHA status/location fields; no network or re-research.

category_l2: The Request constructor accepts any string for the `upgrade` option and only checks its type. `lib/client.js` then appends `connection: upgrade\r\nupgrade: ${upgrade}\r\n` to the request head before the ordinary headers, so CR, LF or NUL bytes in the value terminate or extend the head. An attacker who influences that option can inject arbitrary request headers or smuggle a second request to the origin (the advisory points at non-HTTP services such as Redis, Memcached and Elasticsearch). Ordinary headers already go through `processHeaderValue` and its headerCharRegex in 5.x; the `upgrade` option is the one path that does not. category_l2: The WebSocket receiver parses inbound frames in a loop (ByteParser.run). On a PING frame it consumes the payload, builds a PONG with WebsocketFrameSend and calls this.ws[kResponse].socket.write(frame.createFrame(opcodes.PONG)) (lib/websocket/receiver.js:148 at v5.19.0), then resets the state to INFO and continues while more buffered bytes remain. The value returned by socket.write() is discarded, and nothing consults socket.writableLength / writableNeedDrain, so when the peer never reads the PONGs each additional PING appends another frame to the outbound queue and the parser never yields. Because the PING payload is consumed as application data and the PONG carries it back, inbound bytes and retained outbound bytes are proportional; the vendor describes the attack as asymmetric, with availability the only impact. From 6.x the same write sits in parseControlFrame (line 483 at v6.29.0, line 486 at v7.30.0, line 496 at v8.12.1). The fixes (39f93e14 / 53944624 / b217373b) set #loop = false and register socket.once('drain', ...) when the reply leaves the socket over its high-water mark, bounding the queue.

category_l2: On v5.19.0 the socket 'error' listener registered in lib/client.js (onSocketError, 923-939) opens with assert(err.code !== 'ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID') at line 926. During connect that error code is an expected, handled outcome — the connect-phase branch at 1124-1129 asserts client[kRunning] === 0 and fails the queued requests — so the assert encoded the belief that hostname verification cannot fail after a socket is established. TLS 1.2 renegotiation breaks that belief: Node re-runs checkServerIdentity on the renegotiated handshake, and a server that switches to a same-CA certificate for a different name makes the error arrive on the established socket, where the assert throws. Because it throws inside an EventEmitter listener there is no caller to catch it and the process aborts. Node's TLS stack does not enable renegotiation by default in every build and TLS 1.3 has no renegotiation, which is why the advisory scopes the bug to TLS 1.2. The same assert exists twice in the h2 paths (6.x client-h2.js 139 and 214; 7.x 296 and 439; 8.x 603 and 770) and once in the h1 path (6.x 730, 7.x 931, 8.x 991); b40fbfc0 / 12cfd96c / e257e9f8 delete all of them, leaving only the connect-phase special case.

category_l2: At v5.19.0 the h1 Parser (lib/client.js) accepts any response head the socket yields and attaches it to client[kQueue][client[kRunningIdx]]. onHeadersComplete (680-706) checks only that the socket is alive and that a queue slot exists; it never checks client[kRunning] === 0, i.e. that a request is actually in flight on this socket. After onMessageComplete (828-896) advances kRunningIdx and, for pipelining 1, defers dispatch with setImmediate, an application that issues its next request in that window can have the attacker's already-buffered bytes parsed as that request's response, because kPendingIdx has advanced and kRunningIdx now points at the pending request. The 6.27.0 / 7.28.0 / 8.5.0 fix adds exactly the missing in-flight test (util.destroy(socket, new SocketError('bad response')) when client[kRunning] === 0 in onStatus and onHeadersComplete), marks a socket that has carried a response with kSocketUsed, and makes resumeH1 validate an idle socket (kIdleSocketValidation with a 0 ms timer) before dispatching into it.

category_l2: Rack::Static#applicable_rules evaluates header rules against the PATH_INFO it is handed, which is still URL-encoded, while the file served is resolved from Utils.clean_path_info(Utils.unescape_path(PATH_INFO)); an encoded variant of a static path is therefore served without some of the headers the operator configured for that content class. category_l2: Rack::Directory builds each directory-index row with DIR_FILE, whose anchor is `<a href='%s'>`. The value substituted into href is the file's basename escaped with Rack::Utils.escape_path (which does not escape the ':' of a URI scheme) and then Rack::Utils.escape_html (which escapes quotes, '<' and '>' but does not neutralize a scheme). A file named `javascript:alert(1)` therefore produces href='javascript:alert(1)', which a browser resolves as a JavaScript URL in the listing's origin when a user clicks it

category_l2: Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges parses the HTTP Range header and builds one Range object per comma-separated spec with no upper bound on how many specs it will accept: byte_ranges delegates to get_byte_ranges, which splits $1 on /,\s*/ and loops over every element. The only rejection that depends on the set as a whole is the CVE-2024-26141 total-coverage check (`return [] if ranges.map(&:size).sum > size`), which a header built from many small overlapping specs such as `bytes=0-0,0-0,0-0,...` never trips. A ~200 KB header therefore allocates 200,000 Range objects before the response is even started, and Rack::Files then walks that array again to build a multipart/byteranges body, so one request buys disproportionate CPU, memory, I/O and bandwidth

static_review_summary: The CGI servlet resolves a requested pathInfo by walking the filesystem and derives the CGI script name from the on-disk name (cginameBuilder), so on a case-insensitive file system a request whose pathInfo case differs from the stored file still executes that script while Tomcat matched security constraints against the request URI; constraints that apply to the pathInfo component are therefore bypassed. The cited fix resolves the script through the WebResource API and sets scriptName from the requested urlPath instead of the on-disk cginame, keeping the executed script name consistent with the URI used for constraint matching.
title: Apache Tomcat CGI servlet security constraint bypass (case sensitivity)

static_review_summary: ApplyDiffPatch applies an attacker-controlled patch with git apply --index --cached inside a temporary clone created by t.Clone(ctx, opts.OldBranch, true), i.e. a bare repository. static_review_summary: The /orgs/{org}/labels group in Routes registers the label read endpoints with reqOrgOwnership on mutations but no organization-visibility middleware, so a non-member can GET /api/v1/orgs/{org}/labels and /labels/{id} for a private organization and read label names, colors and descriptions (CWE-200/CWE-862). The cited fix appends reqOrgVisible() to the group; frozen line 1665 is the group registration without it.
title: Gitea: Unauthorized Access to Labels of Private Organizations

admission_checks.notes: fix PR #39839 main ae17c14cffe9, v28 backport 829b49c1ae96. The patch renames the function; the frozen name is home, which encloses line 50.

category_l2: Requesting /{username}/-/repositories for an individual user instead of an organization made the organization home handler dereference a nil organization and pa
static_review_summary: The route /{username}/-/repositories is handled by the organization Repositories handler, which calls home(ctx, true); for an individual user ctx.Org.Organization is nil and home dereferences it, so an unauthenticated request panics and returns 500 repeatedly (CWE-248/CWE-476). The cited fix renames home to orgHome and returns 404 when the organization is nil; frozen line 50 is the unchecked dereference source.
title: Gitea panic on the repositories route of individual users

admission_checks.notes: fix PR #39839/#39847. The anchored group is the one carrying m.Post("/topics", repo.TopicsPost); the same PR adds the cross-origin integration test.

category_l2: POST /{owner}/{repo}/topics was registered without the sign-in middleware that provides the cross-origin protection, so a request issued by a third-party site w
static_review_summary: The POST /{owner}/{repo}/topics group is registered with RepoAssignment, reqRepoAdmin and RepoMustNotBeArchived but not optSignIn, the middleware that provides the CSRF check for cookie-authenticated web POSTs; a third-party page can therefore change a repository's topics for an administrator who visits it (CWE-352). The cited fix adds optSignIn to the group; frozen line 1411 is the route registration.
title: Gitea cross-site request forgery on repository topics

admission_checks.notes: fix PR #39839/#39847; the same helper replaces the equivalent check in ChangeIssueCommentReaction and in the API reaction handlers.

category_l2: The Gitea web handlers for adding and removing reactions on issues and comments did not refuse locked issues for users without write access, although the API di
static_review_summary: ChangeIssueReaction authorizes only signed-in users who can read the issue (or the poster) and never tests issue.IsLocked, so a reader without write access can add or remove reactions on a locked issue and its comments, bypassing the lock's interaction restriction (CWE-863). The cited fix replaces the read check with issue_service.CanSelfChangeOrAccessContent(..., AccessModeRead), which denies locked content to non-writers; frozen line 494 is the read-only check that omits the lock test.
title: Gitea reactions accepted on locked issues and comments

admission_checks.notes: fix PR #39839/#39847. v1.25.5 names the function SearchPublicKeyByContentExact; the 1.27 fix renames it SearchPrincipalKey and adds the type filter.

category_l2: Gitea resolved the principals of an SSH certificate by searching the content of all stored public keys instead of only principal keys. When Gitea trusts a user
static_review_summary: SearchPublicKeyByContentExact looks up a principal by `content = ?` across all stored public keys instead of only principal keys; with SSH_TRUSTED_USER_CA_KEYS configured and SSH_AUTHORIZED_PRINCIPALS_ALLOW=anything, a user can register another user's public key line as their principal and then authenticate as that user through HTTP signatures or the built-in SSH server (CWE-287). The cited fix restricts the query with AND type = KeyTypePrincipal; frozen line 161 is the unfiltered content lookup.
title: Gitea SSH certificate principal impersonation of other users

admission_checks.notes: fix PR #39839/#39847; the addressed variant is re-linking an issue or comment attachment into a release.

static_review_summary: AddReleaseAttachments checks repository and release ownership of an attachment but, for attachments not yet linked to a release, never checks whether it is already linked to an issue or comment; a user with release write access who knows an attachment UUID can link it to a release and then see, rename or delete the private attachment (CWE-639). The cited fix rejects attachments with IssueID, CommentID or ReleaseID set; frozen line 204 is the narrower ReleaseID-only check.
title: Gitea release attachment re-linking of issue attachments

admission_checks.notes: advisory record publishes no FIX reference; the fix was identified by content in the cached commit aab3242f7b96 (PR #38324, 'harden access checks and migration validation'), whose restore.go hunk replaces exactly this call and whose common.go hunk adds the empty-baseURL guard. static_review_summary: The Migration Restore downloader builds each pull request's PatchURL as file:// plus a path from the restored repository's own YAML and then calls CheckAndEnsureSafePR(pr, "", r). CheckAndEnsureSafePR delegates to hasBaseURL, which with an empty baseURL reduces to strings.HasPrefix(toCheck, "") and therefore accepts every URL; the file:// PatchURL is then read from disk during the restore, so a crafted archive can make the server read an arbitrary local file as a PR patch (CWE-22/CWE-73). The cited fix passes "file://"+r.baseDir as the allowed base and makes hasBaseURL answer false for an empty baseURL; frozen line 238 is the call with the empty base.
title: Local File Inclusion via file:// URI in Migration Restore

admission_checks.notes: root cause is a shipped config template, not Go code: the same value also appears in docker/rootless/etc/templates/app.ini:52 and is removed by the same commit. The fix hunk removes both lines verbatim.; functionless_location: the defect is the default value shipped in a Docker app.ini template; the file has no enclosing function

static_review_summary: The Docker image ships a generated app.ini whose [security] section sets REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES = * while also accepting REVERSE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION_USER from the request. Gitea treats every source address as a trusted reverse proxy, so when proxy authentication is enabled any client that can reach the container can set X-WEBAUTH-USER and be authenticated as that user (CWE-290/CWE-306). The cited fix deletes REVERSE_PROXY_LIMIT and REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES from both Docker templates, making reverse-proxy auth opt-in; frozen line 55 is the removed = * default.
title: Gitea Docker image trusts spoofable reverse-proxy headers by default

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) crypto/x509/v3_purp.c:387-387 carry the pre-image (removed_line); 3.5-branch fix 3842516cc15e ("Defer computation of relative CRLDP names") cites the CVE

category_l2: relative CRLDP names resolved eagerly while caching X.509 extensions
static_review_summary: setup_dp() resolves every nameRelativeToCRLIssuer distribution point against the certificate issuer while OpenSSL builds its cached X.509 extension values, so decoding a peer-supplied certificate allocates and re-encodes one X509_NAME per relative CRLDP. A certificate that fits the ~100 KiB accepted peer-certificate budget can drive several hundred MiB of heap growth (CWE-770). The fix defers the relative-name resolution until the distribution point is actually needed for CRL processing; frozen line 387 is the removed eager DIST_POINT_set_dpname() call.
title: Excessive memory allocation in relative CRL distribution point processing

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) ssl/quic/quic_rx_depack.c:1501-1501 carry the pre-image (removed_line); 3.5-branch fix 0fe4442d4f8e ("don't double count full databgram length on unvalidated connections") cites the CVE

category_l2: per-packet credit accounting breaks the 3x RFC 9000 anti-amplification limit
static_review_summary: When the QUIC server runs without client address validation, ossl_quic_handle_frames() adds the length of the whole received datagram to the unvalidated-path credit once per packet that datagram carries, instead of accounting each datagram once. A peer that packs several packets into one datagram therefore inflates the RFC 9000 3x anti-amplification budget in proportion to the packet count (CWE-440), which a spoofing attacker can use for DDoS amplification. The fix deletes the per-packet add_unvalidated_credit() call from frame handling; frozen line 1501 is the removed call.
title: QUIC unvalidated amplification credit over-accounted per packet

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) ssl/quic/quic_sf_list.c:117-118 carry the pre-image (removed_line); 3.5-branch fix ca8402e273af ("New implementation of stream reassembly for QUIC.") cites the CVE

category_l2: head-to-tail linear search in the stream frame list makes reassembly O(n^2)
static_review_summary: ossl_sframe_list_insert() locates the insertion point for an incoming STREAM frame with a head-to-tail linear walk of the fragment list, and only the append case is optimised, so a peer that delivers frames out of order makes every insert O(n) and the reassembly of one connection O(n^2) in the number of buffered fragments (CWE-407). Low attacker bandwidth inside the advertised receive window is enough to burn connection-scoped CPU. The fix replaces the doubly-linked list with the ordered quic_strm_reas implementation; frozen lines 117-118 are the removed walk.
title: Quadratic QUIC stream reassembly on out-of-order frames

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) crypto/ec/ec_mult.c:216-219 carry the pre-image (adjacent_insertion); 3.5-branch fix 3f7e1363dcce ("ec: make ossl_ec_scalar_mul_ladder() scalar padding constant time") cites the CVE; additive fix: bn_set_top_fixed() pins k and lambda before the ladder additions; the frozen lines are the BN_copy() the fix hardens and the arithmetic whose operand tops it fixes

category_l2: scalar padding with value-dependent BIGNUM tops leaks the ECDSA/SM2 nonce
static_review_summary: ossl_ec_scalar_mul_ladder() copies the secret scalar with BN_copy() and then runs the ladder additions on values whose BIGNUM top depends on the scalar magnitude, so the number of words processed - and therefore the signing time - varies with the per-signature nonce for curves that have no dedicated constant-time implementation (CWE-208). Over many signatures this is a lattice / hidden-number-problem key recovery path. The fix pins k and lambda to fixed word counts with bn_set_top_fixed() before the additions; frozen lines 216-219 are the BN_copy() the fix hardens.
title: Timing side channel in generic EC scalar multiplication padding

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) ssl/quic/quic_sf_list.c:42-42 carry the pre-image (structural_shift); 3.5-branch fix 279e7ee1392a ("Limit packet buffer overhead to ~64kB per stream.") cites the CVE; structural shift: the 3.5-branch fix (QUIC_RSTREAM_QPARAM, ~64kB packet-buffer overhead cap per stream) lands in ssl/quic/quic_strm_reas.c, which entered the branch with the CVE-2026-42772 reassembly rewrite, so the diff does not apply textually to the 3.5.8 sf_list implementation; the frozen line is the equivalent retention site (frame keeps the QRX packet ref)

category_l2: stream frames keep the packet buffer reference until the application reads, with no per-stream overhead cap
static_review_summary: stream_frame_new() takes a reference on the QRX packet buffer that carries each STREAM frame, and stream_frame_free() only drops that reference when the application consumes the data or the stream is destroyed. A peer can therefore pin an unbounded number of packet buffers, with the retention time under its own control, by sending stream data the application does not read (CWE-770). The 3.5-branch fix introduces QUIC_RSTREAM_QPARAM and moves chunks off the packet buffer once ~64kB of overhead accumulates per stream; that code lives in ssl/quic/quic_strm_reas.c, which entered the branch with the CVE-2026-42772 reassembly rewrite, so the frozen line 42 is the equivalent retention site in the 3.5.8 implementation.
title: Unbounded QUIC packet buffer retention per stream

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) crypto/ec/ecp_sm2p256.c:283-291 carry the pre-image (removed_line); 3.5-branch fix 469f3e42629f ("Make the ecp_sm2p256 scalar multiplication constant time") cites the CVE

category_l2: is_zeros() branches on secret-derived field elements in the SM2 scalar multiplication
static_review_summary: ecp_sm2p256_point_add() and the neighbouring point routines branch on is_zeros() tests of field elements derived from the secret scalar, so on ARM64 and RISC-V the timing and the cache-line access pattern of SM2 scalar multiplication depend on the private key or the per-signature nonce (CWE-208). The fix removes the is_zeros() special cases and selects results with constant_time_select_64(); frozen lines 283-291 are one of the removed branches.
title: Non-constant-time SM2 point arithmetic on ARM64 and RISC-V

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) ssl/ssl_lib.c:5526-5529 carry the pre-image (adjacent_insertion); 3.5-branch fix 4135f553c9d3 ("Fix out-of-bounds valid_flags access after SSL_set_SSL_CTX()") cites the CVE; additive fix: valid_flags is re-sized when the certificate is swapped in; the frozen line is the cert assignment the inserted resize follows

category_l2: per-connection valid_flags array keeps the old SSL_CTX slot count after the certificate swap
static_review_summary: SSL_set_SSL_CTX() swaps sc->cert for a duplicate of the replacement context's certificate but leaves the per-connection valid_flags array at the size recorded when the connection was created from the original SSL_CTX. If the replacement context knows about more provider TLS-SIGALG entries than the original, later certificate lookups index past the end of that array - an out-of-bounds read and, in some paths, a fixed-value out-of-bounds write on the server heap (CWE-787). The fix re-sizes valid_flags when the certificate is swapped; frozen lines 5526-5529 are the cert swap the inserted resize follows.
title: Out-of-bounds valid_flags access after SSL_set_SSL_CTX() mid-handshake

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) ssl/quic/quic_fc.c:396-397 carry the pre-image (removed_line); 3.5-branch fix 4533ee8a5686 ("CVE-2026-75804 QUIC connection-level flow control not enforced, remote memory exhaustion") cites the CVE

category_l2: stream receive flow control reports only its own error and drops the connection-level violation
static_review_summary: ossl_quic_rxfc_get_error() reports only the stream receiving flow controller's own error code and never consults rxfc->parent, the connection-level controller that owns it. A connection-level flow control violation raised on the parent is therefore invisible to the stream layer, and a peer that stays inside the per-stream window can make the stack hold ~100MB instead of the advertised 768KiB connection window (CWE-770). The fix propagates the parent error code and clears both levels; frozen lines 396-397 are the removed stream-level-only handling.
title: QUIC connection-level flow control not enforced for streams

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) crypto/cmp/cmp_client.c:1002-1002 carry the pre-image (removed_line); 3.5-branch fix 9eb2a8a9b861 ("Guard comparision when values are NULL") cites the CVE

category_l2: response CertId issuer compared without a NULL check when revoking by CSR
static_review_summary: A CMP client that revokes a certificate named by a PKCS#10 CSR (OSSL_CMP_CTX_set1_p10CSR, or `openssl cmp -cmd rr -csr`) has no issuer name, because a CSR does not carry one. When the server names the revoked certificate in its response, OSSL_CMP_exec_RR_ses() hands the response CertId's issuer to X509_NAME_cmp() unconditionally and dereferences the NULL local issuer, crashing the client (CWE-476). The fix guards the comparison for NULL values; frozen line 1002 is the removed unguarded comparison.
title: NULL pointer dereference on CMP revocation responses for a CSR

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) ssl/record/methods/tls1_meth.c:259-261 carry the pre-image (adjacent_insertion); 3.5-branch fix 3a4589d015a9 ("TLS: Reject undersized TLS 1.2 AEAD records before AEAD processing") cites the CVE; additive fix: the guard rejects records shorter than eivlen + taglen before the AEAD branch the frozen lines open

category_l2: record length passed to the AEAD cipher before checking the explicit IV and tag overhead
static_review_summary: tls1_cipher() passes the record length to the AEAD cipher before checking that the record is long enough to contain the explicit IV and the authentication tag. For a DTLS 1.2 datagram whose encrypted fragment is shorter than that overhead the cipher rejects the impossible length, and the resulting failure tears down an established association without any key material (CWE-1284). The fix rejects records shorter than rl->eivlen + rl->taglen before AEAD processing; frozen lines 259-261 open the AEAD branch the inserted guard precedes.
title: Undersized DTLS 1.2 AEAD record tears down an established association

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) crypto/sm2/sm2_sign.c:289-292 carry the pre-image (removed_line); 3.5-branch fix 6b90445a56b9 ("sm2: make sm2_sig_gen() constant time") cites the CVE

category_l2: variable-time BIGNUM arithmetic on the secret nonce and private key in sm2_sig_gen
static_review_summary: sm2_sig_gen() computes r + k and the rest of the signature value with variable-time BIGNUM operations on the per-signature nonce and the private key, so the time taken to produce an SM2 signature depends on those secret values (CWE-208). Over many signatures the nonce leaks through a lattice / hidden-number-problem attack. The fix makes the signing arithmetic constant time; frozen lines 289-292 are the removed variable-time BN_add() on the nonce.
title: Timing side channel in SM2 signature generation

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) ssl/statem/statem_dtls.c:1218-1219 carry the pre-image (adjacent_insertion); 3.5-branch fix 906cf0ef1c85 ("dtls: reset init_off before retransmitting a message") cites the CVE; additive fix: init_off is reset right after the frozen memcpy and the retransmit timer is skipped while a write is parked

category_l2: retransmit path leaves init_off from a suspended write and overwrites parked write state
static_review_summary: dtls1_retransmit_message() rebuilds a queued handshake message into s->init_buf and leaves s->init_off wherever a suspended write left it. A retransmit that fires while a write is parked mid-fragment therefore resumes from a stale offset: the message can be read past the end of the buffer, and the retransmission overwrites s->init_off / init_num that the parked write needs to resume (CWE-125). The fix resets init_off to the start of the message when retransmitting and skips the retransmit timer while a write is still parked; frozen lines 1218-1219 are the memcpy the inserted reset follows.
title: DTLS retransmission rebuilds a handshake message from a stale buffer offset

admission_checks.notes: frozen 3.5.8 line(s) ssl/quic/quic_channel.c:3384-3388 carry the pre-image (removed_line); 3.5-branch fix dba3c48d653c ("CVE-2026-84784 QUIC: unbounded RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID backlog (memory DoS)") cites the CVE

category_l2: cur_retire_prior_to advanced before the retire frames are sent, so retire frames queue without a cap
static_review_summary: ossl_quic_channel_on_new_conn_id() walks from ch->cur_retire_prior_to up to the peer-supplied Retire Prior To value, enqueues one RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame per step and advances ch->cur_retire_prior_to immediately, before any of those frames is sent. A peer that floods NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames with increasing Retire Prior To values therefore pushes an unbounded backlog of retire frames into the channel frame queue and exhausts local memory (CWE-770). The fix advances only a local counter and moves cur_retire_prior_to forward when the queued frame is freed; frozen lines 3384-3388 are the removed unbounded loop.
title: Unbounded RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID backlog from NEW_CONNECTION_ID floods

admission_checks.notes: frozen 8.3.0 line(s) lib/fopen.c:71-71 carry the pre-image of fix 73b65e94f353 ("fopen: create short(er) temporary file name") (removed_line); curl advisory SEMVER 7.84.0..8.5.0 and the NVD CPE match agree; curl-8_5_0 ships the fixed code and the frozen tree does not

category_l2: HSTS store rewritten through a temp name derived from the target name
static_review_summary: Curl_fopen() derives the temporary file name by appending a random suffix to the full target path (frozen line 71: aprintf("%s.%s.tmp", filename, randsuffix)). When the target file name is long enough that the derived temp name exceeds the file-system NAME_MAX, the temp file cannot be created and the HSTS store rewrite path clears the existing HSTS file, so a later curl invocation trusts HSTS hosts that the store should have pinned (CWE-311). NVD CPE and the curl advisory both place 8.3.0 in 7.84.0 <= v < 8.5.0. The fix (73b65e94, released in 8.5.0) replaces the target-name-derived temp name with a directory prefix plus 40 random characters and ".tmp", via the new dirslash() helper; curl-8_5_0 ships that code and the frozen 8.3.0 tree does not.
title: HSTS file contents cleared when the target file name is too long

admission_checks.notes: frozen 8.3.0 line(s) lib/setopt.c:2693-2698 carry the pre-image of fix 17d302e56221 ("setopt: Fix disabling all protocols") (removed_line); curl advisory SEMVER 7.85.0..8.7.0 and the NVD CPE match agree; curl-8_7_0 ships the fixed code and the frozen tree does not

category_l2: protocol allow-list keeps its default when the parsed mask is empty
static_review_summary: Curl_vsetopt() parses CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS_STR into a local curl_prot_t and assigns data->set.allowed_protocols only when protocol2num() succeeds (frozen lines 2693-2698). protocol2num() returns CURLE_BAD_FUNCTION_ARGUMENT when the parsed mask is empty (frozen lines 183-186), which is exactly the "-all,-http" case, so the caller keeps the default protocol set and the explicitly disabled protocols stay usable (CWE-115/CWE-436 misinterpretation of the option value). The fix (17d302e5, released in 8.7.0) passes the destination mask directly to protocol2num() and clears it before parsing, so the empty set survives the error path; curl-8_7_0 ships that code and the frozen 8.3.0 tree does not.

category_l2: stapled OCSP response only parsed when GnuTLS reports it unchecked
static_review_summary: Curl_gtls_verifyserver() parses the stapled OCSP response only when gnutls_ocsp_status_request_is_checked() returns 0 (frozen line 928); when GnuTLS reports the response as already checked, the else branch at frozen lines 1024-1025 records "server certificate status verification OK" without inspecting the OCSP certificate status, so a response whose status is an error other than revoked (for example unauthorized) is accepted as valid (CWE-295). category_l2: PUSH_PROMISE header array freed without its header strings
static_review_summary: on_header() doubles the PUSH_PROMISE header array as headers arrive; once the allocation count exceeds 1000 it frees the array with Curl_safefree() and aborts the push (frozen line 1458). Curl_safefree() frees only the array block, not the up-to-1000 header strings it holds, and push_headers_used keeps its value, so every aborted push leaks its headers and the error is silent (CWE-772). The fix (deca8039, released in 8.7.0) adds free_push_headers(), which frees each used string and resets the counter, and calls it on the too-many-headers path, the realloc failure path and stream teardown; curl-8_7_0 ships that code and the frozen 8.3.0 tree does not.

static_review_summary: AddPackageTag() reads the dist-tag publish body with io.ReadAll(ctx.Req.Body) and no size bound (frozen routers/api/packages/npm/npm.go:336); the body is only a quoted version string, so an authenticated package owner can post an arbitrarily large body and exhaust the process memory (CWE-770). static_review_summary: showUserFeed() derives includePrivate from organisation membership and passes it straight into feed_service.GetFeeds(GetFeedsOptions{IncludePrivate: includePrivate}) (frozen routers/web/feed/profile.go:44-48); it never consults the API token scope, so a public-only token still receives private activity of its owner, the same confinement #37698 added elsewhere (CWE-200/CWE-862). category_l2: one allowed A record lets a host with a blocked second answer pass validation
static_review_summary: checkByAllowBlockList() starts ipAllowed at false and ORs each resolved address (frozen services/migrations/migrate.go:89-94), so a hostname whose DNS answer contains one allow-listed address and one blocked/internal address passes validation whenever the host name itself is not allow-listed; Init() also never adds private/loopback networks to the block list when AllowLocalNetworks=false (frozen lines 494-497) (CWE-918/CWE-200). category_l2: case-insensitive LIKE lookup matches a case variant of a victim public key
static_review_summary: The built-in SSH server authenticates by looking the presented key up with `content LIKE ?` (frozen models/asymkey/ssh_key.go:145), which is case-insensitive on SQLite and other databases, so a case variant of another user's registered RSA key whose private key the attacker can derive matches the victim account (CWE-287). The fixed release postdates v1.27.0, so the evidence is the fingerprint lookup the patch adds in place of the LIKE comparison.
