category_l2: deploy-key push recorded as the repository owner
static_review_summary: When the hook pipeline resolves the pusher it looks up opts.PusherID as a user (frozen services/repository/push.go:113 for tag refs and :160 for branches; the pusher was already populated with the repository owner by the SSH/HTTP layer for deploy keys), so protected-tag allow lists and push-option permission checks evaluate the owner instead of the deploy key, letting a writable deploy key create protected tags and flip repository visibility (CWE-863). category_l2: duplicate tree entries let review and checkout see different content
static_review_summary: syncGitConfig sets core.commitGraph and the other runtime options but never enables object consistency checks (frozen modules/git/config.go:56), so a push can store a tree with two entries of the same name, which Git considers inconsistent: the web diff and file views resolve the first entry while checkout, Gitea Actions and release archives use the last, letting a contributor show benign content in review while CI executes attacker-controlled content (CWE-436). The fix sets transfer.fsckObjects=true, with the Gitaly ignore list for harmless historic objects, for every repository.

category_l2: external tracker regex with alternating capture groups panics the renderer
static_review_summary: FindRenderizableReferenceRegexp assumes capture group 2 always participated in the match and slices content with match[2]:match[3] (frozen modules/references/references.go:381-383), so an external issue-tracker pattern whose alternatives place the reference in a later group, for example (A-(\d+)|B-(\d+)), yields -1 and panics with an invalid slice index whenever matching content is rendered, crashing the instance for every user (CWE-129). The fix scans the group pairs for the first group that participated and returns nil when none did.

category_l2: Unchecked UTF-16 high surrogate accepted by the tokenizer
static_review_summary: The UTF-16 encodings report a 4-byte character (BT_LEAD4) for a high surrogate but never verify that the next code unit is a low surrogate: xmltok_impl.c falls back to `#define IS_INVALID_CHAR(enc, ptr, n) (0)` for them and the little2/big2 vtables carry NULL for isInvalid4 (frozen expat/lib/xmltok.c:825). A lone high surrogate therefore consumes the following code unit, so a following `<` is hidden from the tokenizer and unpaired surrogates reach XML_UNICODE applications (CWE-20). The fix adds LITTLE2_IS_INVALID_CHAR/BIG2_IS_INVALID_CHAR and swaps NULL_VTABLE for UTF16_NULL_VTABLE, whose isInvalid4 is real. The fix site is a file-scope vtable initializer, hence no enclosing function.
title: Unchecked UTF-16 high surrogate accepted by the tokenizer

category_l2: Hash flooding from a 4-to-8-byte SipHash salt
static_review_summary: Hash flooding protection derives the SipHash key from m_hash_secret_salt, an unsigned long of 4 bytes on ILP32 and 8 bytes elsewhere, and copy_salt_to_sipkey puts that single word in k[1] with k[0] = 0 (frozen expat/lib/xmlparse.c:7156-7157). SipHash accepts 16 bytes, so only 32 to 64 bits of the key are unknown and a crafted document can collide hash-table entries to degrade parsing to quadratic time (CWE-331/CWE-407). The fix stores a full struct sipkey in m_hash_secret_salt_128, fills 16 bytes of entropy, and adds XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes; the removed k[0] = 0 / k[1] = get_hash_secret_salt(parser) pair is the pre-image.

category_l2: Multipart parse failure leaves temporary upload files on disk
static_review_summary: Request.parseParts holds the FileItem list in a try block and never records it for the failure path, so when parsing throws (including when a configured limit is exceeded) the temporary copies already written by the multipart parser are only reclaimed by garbage collection. A client can stream uploads that fail the limit check faster than GC removes the files and fill the work directory, exhausting disk and taking the process down. The fix hoists the list out of the try block and adds a finally that clears the parts and calls delete() on every FileItem when parsing did not succeed.
title: Multipart parse failure leaves temporary upload files on disk

category_l2: Chunk extensions are not validated, allowing HTTP request smuggling
static_review_summary: ChunkedInputFilter treats everything after the first semicolon of a chunk header as an opaque extension: it just counts bytes and never checks the extension grammar, and the counted size is compared against maxExtensionSize only after the fact. category_l2: Authenticated WebSocket session outlives its HTTP session
static_review_summary: WsServerContainer keys authenticated WebSocket sessions by the HTTP session id and only removes them when the WebSocket itself closes or the container is stopped. When the HTTP session times out or is invalidated, the WebSocket session whose principal came from it stays open and keeps the authenticated identity, so a shared or expired browser session leaves a usable authenticated channel behind; a new HTTP session that reuses the id can also attach to the old WebSocket. The fix registers a session listener on the HTTP session and closes/binds the WebSocket sessions when that session ends.
title: Authenticated WebSocket session outlives its HTTP session

category_l2: Bad OR handling when evaluating RewriteRule conditions
static_review_summary: RewriteRule.evaluate evaluates a condition and, when it matches, skips every following condition marked [OR] with a while loop that runs even when the matching condition was not itself an OR member. The rule immediately after an OR group is therefore dropped from evaluation and the substitution is applied even though a condition that must hold for the rule did not run, which lets a crafted request reach a target the rewrite configuration was meant to guard. The byte at decoded_string[0] is therefore left as whatever the previous iteration wrote (the "~" itself, or the preceding character), so a path such as "/a~1b" names "~a/b"-style keys rather than "a/b" and cJSONUtils_ApplyPatches add/remove/replace/move operations act on a key the caller did not address, silently corrupting or deleting unintended members (CVE-2026-29036, CWE-706, affects 1.5.0 through 1.7.19). The same line is still present in master (2026-10-31), so there is no fix to diff against; the probe is the advisory text against the frozen source.
title: cJSON decodes a JSON Pointer ~1 escape into the wrong output byte

category_l2: cJSON_Compare recurses into every object subtree in both directions
static_review_summary: The cJSON_Object branch of cJSON_Compare walks a's members comparing each against b and then walks b's members comparing each against a, recursing into every shared subtree once per direction. The work therefore multiplies by the branching factor squared at every level, so a small, deeply nested document (depth around 40) compared for equality against a structurally equal reference burns hours of CPU, and the cost doubles per added level; the function has no depth bound, unlike the parser's 1000-level nesting limit. Any application that calls cJSON_Compare on attacker-influenced JSON is exposed to algorithmic-complexity denial of service (CVE-2026-67216, CWE-407, through 1.7.19).
title: cJSON_Compare recurses into every object subtree in both directions

category_l2: cJSON JSON Patch replace and move destroy the target before validation
static_review_summary: apply_patch handles REPLACE by detaching and deleting the existing member (lines 890-895) before it resolves the patch's "value" member, so a replace operation that omits value returns status 7 after the target member has already been deleted; MOVE likewise detaches the source subtree (line 918) before the destination parent is resolved, and a move whose destination cannot be resolved returns status 9 and deletes the detached subtree in cleanup. In both cases cJSONUtils_ApplyPatches mutates and destroys addressable members of the target document even though it returns a failure status, defeating the all-or-nothing contract callers rely on to reject bad patches (CVE-2026-67217, CWE-696, through 1.7.19).

affected_range: cJSON 1.7.15 (CVE record); the bounded 64-byte copy is unchanged in v1.7.16
category_l2: cJSON parse_number truncates number literals longer than 63 bytes
static_review_summary: parse_number copies the number literal into a fixed 64-byte stack buffer and stops after 63 bytes (line 309 and the bounded loop at line 321). For a grammar-valid document whose number literal is longer than 63 characters, strtod sees only the truncated prefix and input_buffer->offset advances by that prefix length, so the remaining digits are then parsed as trailing garbage and cJSON_Parse rejects a document that other conforming parsers accept (the advisory's data-out-of-sync / denial-of-service case). The bounded copy is unchanged from v1.7.15 through v1.7.19 and master, so the behaviour is present at the frozen v1.7.16 (CVE-2023-26819, CWE-440).
title: cJSON parse_number truncates number literals longer than 63 bytes

category_l2: pkcs12_key_certificate_mismatch
static_review_summary: serialize_key_and_certificates_to_pkcs12 builds the PKCS#12 structure with PKCS12_create (backend.py:1812) and then, when an hmac_hash override is in effect, feeds the result straight to PKCS12_set_mac at backend.py:1829. category_l2: rsa_pkcs1v15_padding_oracle
static_review_summary: _enc_dec_rsa_pkey_ctx is the whole RSA encrypt/decrypt path of the OpenSSL backend: it sets the padding mode on the EVP_PKEY context, calls EVP_PKEY_decrypt, and at rsa.py:162-163 turns every non-positive return value into ValueError("Encryption/decryption failed."). PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption fails exactly when the recovered block does not carry valid 0x00 0x02 padding, so the exception (and its timing, measured at roughly 400 ns in pyca issue 9785) separates valid from invalid padding and yields the Bleichenbacher oracle that the CVE-2020-25659 fix did not close. cryptography 42.0.0 moved the path to Rust and, more importantly, shipped wheels built against OpenSSL 3.2.0, whose implicit rejection stops EVP_PKEY_decrypt from reporting padding failures; the advisory range 0 < 42.0.0 covers 41.0.5 (CVE-2023-50782, CWE-203). The sdist source at this tag is the code line the advisory describes, so the row is anchored on the Python path rather than on the wheel.
title: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption raises a distinguishable error on a padding failure

category_l2: ec_subgroup_validation
static_review_summary: EllipticCurvePublicNumbers.public_key() reaches load_elliptic_curve_public_numbers (backend.py:1093) and then _ec_key_set_public_key_affine_coordinates, which at backend.py:1248 installs the point with EC_POINT_set_affine_coordinates and at backend.py:1254 with EC_KEY_set_public_key. category_l2: protocol_relative_url_adopted_as_ssr_hostname
static_review_summary: ServerPlatformLocation builds its state from INITIAL_CONFIG.url through parseUrl (location.ts:23), which resolves the untrusted string against the synthetic base "resolve://" with new URL (location.ts:31-34). A request URL such as "//attacker.example/app" is parsed as protocol-relative: hostname becomes attacker.example while the protocol maps back to "" at location.ts:38, and the constructor copies hostname/pathname/port into PlatformLocation (location.ts:69-77). Any same-origin decision or URL built from PlatformLocation.hostname therefore uses the attacker domain. The 19.x fix f3a5bfb (2026-04-14, shipped in 19.2.21) rewrites parseUrl to prepend the document origin whenever the input starts with "/" so the host cannot be replaced; its regression test asserts hostname "" and pathname equal to the raw input for ["/\\attacker.com/deep/path", "//attacker.com/deep/path"]. The pre-image of that fix is this exact file. At 19.2.15 the resolution runs against the non-special resolve: base, so the backslash spelling alone does not produce a foreign host (node: new URL("/\\evil.com/", "resolve://").hostname === ""), while the protocol-relative spelling does (new URL("//evil.com/x", "resolve://").hostname === "evil.com"). Advisory range 19.0.0-next.0 < 19.2.21 covers 19.2.15 (CVE-2026-41423, CWE-918).
title: SSR URL resolution adopts the host of a protocol-relative request URL as the platform hostname

category_l2: 32_bit_transfer_cache_key_collision
static_review_summary: makeCacheKey joins method, responseType, mapped URL, serialized body and sorted query parameters into one string (transfer_cache.ts:266-283) and hashes it with generateHash (transfer_cache.ts:293-305). category_l2: hpack_metadata_size_accounted_per_frame
static_review_summary: EmitHeader adds each parsed field to *frame_length_ and compares the running total with metadata_size_limit_ (hpack_parser.cc:1049-1055). frame_length_ is zeroed in BeginFrame (hpack_parser.cc:1282), and BeginFrame runs for every CONTINUATION frame as well as the initial HEADERS frame (parsing.cc:346 calls init_header_frame_parser(t, 1), which reaches BeginFrame at parsing.cc:623) while metadata_buffer_ keeps pointing at the same batch. The limit is therefore applied per frame, not per header block, and an attacker can chain unlimited CONTINUATION frames that each add up to the per-frame budget to the same metadata batch. The check also runs only after the field value has been buffered: ParseUncompressed (hpack_parser.cc:795-810) waits for the full declared string length before the size accounting happens, and ParseVarint (hpack_parser.cc:503-554) reads an unbounded run of 0x80 continuation bytes. The 1.53.2 security backport 6bb17232 (PR #33021, 2023-05-10; master PR #33597) replaces this accounting with RandomEarlyDetection soft/hard limits computed over the whole header block and rejects oversized metadata before the value is buffered; neither src/core/lib/backoff/random_early_detection.h nor the HpackParseResult type exists in the frozen tree. GHSA-496j-2rq6-j6cc ranges 0<1.53.2, 1.54.0<1.54.3, 1.55.0<1.55.2 and 1.56.0<1.56.2; v1.52.0 is in the first band (CVE-2023-33953, CWE-400).

category_l2: accept_emfile_tears_down_listener
static_review_summary: on_read loops on grpc_accept4 and only re-arms the listener read closure for EINTR and for EAGAIN/ECONNABORTED/EWOULDBLOCK (tcp_server_posix.cc:203-208). Every other errno, including EMFILE and ENFILE, falls into the else branch at tcp_server_posix.cc:209-221, logs "Failed accept4" and jumps to the error label at line 296, which merely decrements active_ports (and deactivates all ports only when the server is already shutting down) and returns without calling grpc_fd_notify_on_read. The listener is left with no pending read notification, so after an attacker exhausts the process file-descriptor table with connection attempts the server stops accepting for the rest of its lifetime even though the fd limit is transient. admission_checks.notes: Frozen v4.15.2 middleware/proxy.go:386-391 at 25685e6f5f7b is the vulnerable pre-image. Fix 3fb0ba7e1764 is 24 commits ahead of the frozen SHA (v4.16.1 tag commit 600b9855df). Published range: >= 4.0.0, < 4.16.1 (Go github.com/labstack/echo/v4; frozen v4.15.2 in range); advisory is published and not withdrawn (no_counter_evidence), the cited construct is present (component_present), and the frozen SHA is the v4.15.2 tag commit inside the v4 range (sha_release_match). If the upstream answers with an ordinary HTTP response and keeps the connection alive, proxyRaw keeps tunnelling and subsequent requests on that connection reach the upstream without passing through the Echo router or its route/group middleware, so authentication enforced only there is bypassed (CWE-444, CWE-863). static_review_summary: proxyRaw (middleware/proxy.go:134) hijacks the client connection, dials the upstream and copies both directions, then waits for both goroutines at lines 176-181 without closing the other side when one direction ends. title: Unbounded response cookies risk denial of service in guzzlehttp/guzzle
category_l2: unbounded Set-Cookie fields serialised into one Cookie header

admission_checks.notes: Frozen guzzle/guzzle 7.14.1 at 6b1d2429a2c312474c523aa9017fba0c07b5f4a0; fix 7b68220d6543 is the 7.15.1 release commit (compare: 38 ahead, 0 behind the frozen SHA) and its hunks for CookieJar.php, SetCookie.php and RedirectMiddleware.php apply cleanly with git apply --check. withCookieHeader() is reached unchanged by the fix hunk and has no length/count accounting.

static_review_summary: CookieJar accepts an unlimited number of Set-Cookie fields of unlimited size from one response and later serialises every match into one Cookie header with no length or count cap: extractCookies() stores each cookie unconditionally and withCookieHeader() appends name=value pairs without tracking the header length (src/Cookie/CookieJar.php:291-301). A malicious server can therefore drive memory growth and emit a Cookie header that later handlers, proxies or origins reject. The 7.15.1 fix adds MAX_SET_COOKIE_FIELD_LENGTH/MAX_SET_COOKIE_FIELDS in extractCookies() and MAX_REQUEST_COOKIES/MAX_COOKIE_HEADER_LENGTH in withCookieHeader().

title: URI fragments disclosed in redirect Referer headers in guzzlehttp/guzzle

admission_checks.notes: Frozen guzzle/guzzle 7.14.1 at 6b1d2429a2c312474c523aa9017fba0c07b5f4a0; fix 7b68220d6543 is the 7.15.1 release commit (compare: 38 ahead, 0 behind the frozen SHA) and its hunks for CookieJar.php, SetCookie.php and RedirectMiddleware.php apply cleanly with git apply --check. The 7.15.1 fix adds withFragment("") before serialising the URI.

admission_checks.notes: Frozen guzzle/guzzle 7.14.1 at 6b1d2429a2c312474c523aa9017fba0c07b5f4a0; fix 744101956d78 is the 7.15.2 release commit (compare: 40 ahead, 0 behind). admission_checks.notes: Frozen guzzle/guzzle 7.14.1 at 6b1d2429a2c312474c523aa9017fba0c07b5f4a0; fix 744101956d78 is the 7.15.2 release commit (compare: 40 ahead, 0 behind). static_review_summary: CurlFactory::getDefaultConf() gives libcurl the request URI as text in CURLOPT_URL while the request headers (including Host) are passed separately in _headers (src/Handler/CurlFactory.php:1744-1747); libcurl percent-decodes and IDNA-maps the authority itself and connects to that host while the origin receives the unnormalised Host value. title: Greedy multipart boundary parsing selects the last boundary parameter

admission_checks.notes: Frozen rack/rack v3.1.13 at 037953789da9cd49c4a3453ade6ede13619276e0. The advisory carries three branch rows; the 3.1 row is the one that contains this tag. Fix 10626530f3 (3.1.21) has two hunks. Hunk 2 (the guard that rejects whitespace and a duplicate boundary, returning data[2]) applies to the frozen tree at parser.rb:81 with offset -23. Hunk 1 fails only because its context carries FWS and HEADER_VALUE, constants introduced with the 3.1.16 header-regex anchoring (CVE-2025-49007); the MULTIPART line it rewrites is present verbatim at parser.rb:34, and no whitespace or duplicate-boundary guard exists in the frozen file.

static_review_summary: Rack::Multipart::Parser.parse_boundary matches the Content-Type with the greedy MULTIPART regex (lib/rack/multipart/parser.rb:34) "\Amultipart/.*boundary=\"?([^\";,]+)\"?" and returns capture group 1 (parser.rb:84). The leading ".*" is greedy, so a header containing several boundary parameters resolves to the last one, while an intermediary that honours the first parameter inspects a different body structure than the one Rack parses. title: Escape-heavy quoted multipart parameters cause super-linear parsing

admission_checks.notes: Frozen rack/rack v3.1.13 at 037953789da9cd49c4a3453ade6ede13619276e0. The advisory carries three branch rows; the 3.1 row is the one that contains this tag. Fix 17ce7836be (3.1.21) has three hunks. Hunk 3, the escape counter and raise inside the quoted-value loop, applies to the frozen tree at parser.rb:347 with offset -57. Hunk 1 needs PARSER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT and hunk 2 needs @total_bytes_read, both introduced by CVE-2026-34829 in the same release. The frozen file has no @content_disposition_quoted_escapes or CONTENT_DISPOSITION_QUOTED_ESCAPES_LIMIT (grep, 0 hits), so the unbounded loop is present as described.

static_review_summary: Rack::Multipart::Parser#handle_mime_head parses a quoted Content-Disposition parameter by repeatedly searching for the next quote or backslash with String#index, copying the prefix into a new string and deleting it with String#slice! (parser.rb:337-358). Each escape therefore re-scans and re-copies the remaining value, so a part whose name is a long run of backslash escapes costs super-linear time; with up to 4095 parts per request and a 1536-byte disposition cap the work stays within the default limits while the CPU cost grows with the square of the escape count. The 3.1.21 fix counts quoted escapes and raises Error once they pass CONTENT_DISPOSITION_QUOTED_ESCAPES_LIMIT (8 KiB).

admission_checks.notes: Frozen rack/rack v3.1.13 at 037953789da9cd49c4a3453ade6ede13619276e0. The advisory carries three branch rows; the 3.1 row is the one that contains this tag. The root is a developer-configured filesystem path that was expanded with File.expand_path and is interpolated into the regex without Regexp.escape, so metacharacters such as "+", "*" or "." change the match: the prefix is not removed and the absolute filesystem path is rendered into the directory listing HTML, exposing deployment layout. title: Multipart parsing without Content-Length allows unbounded chunked uploads
category_l2: no total byte limit on multipart bodies read without Content-Length

admission_checks.notes: Frozen rack/rack v3.1.13 at 037953789da9cd49c4a3453ade6ede13619276e0. The advisory carries three branch rows; the 3.1 row is the one that contains this tag. Fix 367a2a0ec6 (3.1.21) has five hunks. Hunk 2 (the parse() Content-Length check), hunk 4 (initialize) and hunk 5 (the read_data accounting) apply to the frozen tree at 90, 215 and 258 with offsets -35, -42 and -43. Hunk 1 (the constant) and hunk 3 need BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT and @body_retained/@retained_size, added by CVE-2025-61771 in 3.1.17. The frozen file has no PARSER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (grep, 0 hits) and BoundedIO is still conditional on content_length at parser.rb:99.

static_review_summary: Rack::Multipart::Parser.parse wraps the body in BoundedIO only when content_length is non-nil (parser.rb:99), and read_data (parser.rb:258-261) reads @bufsize bytes per call with no cumulative accounting. A chunked multipart/form-data request without Content-Length therefore streams to disk through Tempfile with no total byte limit, so an unauthenticated client can fill the disk. The 3.1.21 fix adds PARSER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (10 GiB default, RACK_MULTIPART_PARSER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT), rejects a declared Content-Length above it in parse(), and counts bytes read in read_data.

title: Quadratic Accept-Encoding expansion in Rack::Utils.select_best_encoding
category_l2: wildcard expansion rescans the whole Accept-Encoding list on every wildcard entry

admission_checks.notes: Frozen rack/rack v3.1.13 at 037953789da9cd49c4a3453ade6ede13619276e0. The advisory carries three branch rows; the 3.1 row is the one that contains this tag. Fix 55db26e7f4 (3.1.21) applies cleanly to the frozen tree with git apply --check; the frozen file has no wildcard_seen variable and no accept_encoding[0...16] truncation (grep, 0 hits).

static_review_summary: Rack::Utils.select_best_encoding expands Accept-Encoding entries and, for every wildcard entry, recomputes accept_encoding.map(&:first) inside the loop (lib/rack/utils.rb:197-207). With N wildcard entries that is N scans of the parsed header, i.e. quadratic work, and the resulting expanded list is then walked again with per-entry delete. Rack::Deflater calls the method for every response when enabled, so one request with a crafted Accept-Encoding header burns CPU. The 3.1.21 fix truncates the parsed header to the first 16 encodings, expands the wildcard at most once, and replaces sort_by with a comparator that keeps the existing ordering.

title: Forwarded header semicolon splitting enables host and scheme spoofing
category_l2: quoted semicolons in Forwarded are re-split as directives, smuggling host/proto past a proxy

admission_checks.notes: Frozen rack/rack v3.1.13 at 037953789da9cd49c4a3453ade6ede13619276e0. The advisory carries three branch rows; the 3.1 row is the one that contains this tag. Fix 9df5d34d4f (3.1.21) applies cleanly to the frozen tree with git apply --check; the frozen implementation is exactly the split-on-semicolon shape quoted in the advisory, and ALLOWED_FORWARED_PARAMS is absent (grep, 0 hits).

static_review_summary: Rack::Utils.forwarded_values splits the RFC 7239 Forwarded header on ";" before it parses individual name=value pairs (lib/rack/utils.rb:153) and then splits each field on "," and "=". A quoted value may legally contain semicolons, so Forwarded: for="127.0.0.1;host=evil.com;proto=https" is read as several directives instead of one quoted for value. In deployments where an upstream proxy or WAF validates the quoted value as a single string, the client smuggles host, proto, for or by parameters past that inspection and Rack applies them to the request URL. The 3.1.21 fix replaces the split-based scan with a stateful parser that handles quoted strings and backslash escapes, allows only by/for/host/proto through ALLOWED_FORWARED_PARAMS, and caps parameters and escapes at 1024.

title: obs-fold multipart headers keep CRLF in parsed parameter values
category_l2: obs-fold CRLF survives multipart header unfolding into filename/name values

admission_checks.notes: Frozen rack/rack v3.1.13 at 037953789da9cd49c4a3453ade6ede13619276e0. The advisory carries three branch rows; the 3.1 row is the one that contains this tag. Fix ae320b4661 is the 3-1-stable backport of the 3.2 fix and applies to the frozen tree at parser.rb:303 with offset -57 (git apply --check). The frozen file has no OBS_UNFOLD constant and no unfolding gsub (grep, 0 hits). This advisory is the only one of the eight whose 3.1 row runs to < 3.1.22.

static_review_summary: Rack::Multipart::Parser#handle_mime_head extracts the part Content-Type and Content-Disposition values from the folded header block (parser.rb:309-311) and passes them straight to the parameter scanner, with no RFC 5322 Section 2.2.3 obs-fold unfolding. A header such as filename="test\r\n foo.txt" therefore yields a parsed filename that still contains CRLF, and an application that reuses that value in a response header is exposed to header injection or response splitting. The 3-1-stable backport adds OBS_UNFOLD = \r\n([ \t]) and gsubs both the content type and the disposition before scanning.

title: Content-Length uses character count in Rack::Files error responses
category_l2: Content-Length computed with String#size understates the multibyte error body

admission_checks.notes: Frozen rack/rack v3.1.13 at 037953789da9cd49c4a3453ade6ede13619276e0. The advisory carries three branch rows; the 3.1 row is the one that contains this tag. Fix c3645d377f (3.1.21) applies cleanly to the frozen tree with git apply --check; files.rb:197 is the only body.size.to_s site in the frozen file.

static_review_summary: Rack::Files#fail builds the 404/405 response headers with CONTENT_LENGTH => body.size.to_s (lib/rack/files.rb:197). String#size counts characters, not bytes, so a body containing multibyte UTF-8 declares a Content-Length smaller than the bytes actually written. Rack::Files reflects the decoded request path in its error body, so a request for a missing path with percent-encoded UTF-8 characters triggers the mismatch, and a server that frames the response from the header desynchronises the connection. The 3.1.21 fix switches to body.bytesize.

title: WebSocket ByteParser folds the 64-bit frame length with (upper << 8) + lower
category_l2: 64-bit frame length is folded with a signed 32-bit shift and only the upper word is validated

admission_checks.notes: Frozen nodejs/undici v5.19.0 at f5c89e5c87c7d702996b152c4ad86302b60c4181. The advisory has no commit references; the fix was recovered from the v6.23.0...v6.24.0 compare (commit 5a97f089 "Fix websocket 64-bit length overflow", receiver.js +3/-4). The 6.23.0 pre-image is byte-identical in the changed lines to the frozen 5.19.0 code ((upper > 2 ** 31 - 1) guard, then payloadLength = (upper << 8) + lower); the fixed version tests (upper !== 0 || lower > 2 ** 31 - 1) and assigns lower. The vendor rows are >=6.0.0,<6.24.0 and >=7.0.0,<7.24.0; the lower bound is extended to 0.0.0 because the same code ships in 5.x and the 5.x line has no fix (the CVE-2026-1527 row in this dataset uses the same convention).

static_review_summary: ByteParser.run parses the 64-bit extended payload length as (upper << 8) + lower after rejecting only upper > 2^31 - 1 (lib/websocket/receiver.js:194-216 at v5.19.0). The shift is not a multiply by 2^32 and JavaScript turns it into a signed 32-bit value, so any upper word above 2^23 - 1 overflows to a negative or truncated payloadLength; the parser then leaves READ_DATA with a bogus length, consumes the wrong number of bytes from the socket buffer and the client throws an uncaught TypeError that terminates the process. A malicious WebSocket server chooses the length. The 6.24.0 fix rejects any non-zero upper word or lower > 2^31 - 1 and uses lower directly (5a97f0893b53ba7d1d5549d3df7e55d9c2673f89). The 5.x line has no fix.

title: oneshot State::set_complete publishes VALUE_SENT on an already-closed channel
category_l2: State::set_complete sets VALUE_SENT with fetch_or even when CLOSED is already set, so sender and receiver access the value UnsafeCell at the same time

admission_checks.notes: Frozen tokio-rs/tokio tokio-1.8.0 at 677107d8d9278265798c5efdc75374a25b41a4b8. The advisory has no commit references; the real fix e0cf906ae161a8714711a2baeac7713eaeaae2 ("sync: fix racy UnsafeCell access on a closed oneshot (#4226)") was recovered from the tokio-1.8.3...tokio-1.8.4 compare. The OSV GIT fixed events in this record (2273eb1a, 2a3c803d) are "chore: fix CI on master (#4008)" and "chore: prepare Tokio v1.8.4 release", not code fixes. The oneshot.rs fix patch applies cleanly to the frozen 1.8.0 tree (git apply --check rc=0). Vendor rows are >=0.1.14,<1.8.4 and >=1.9.0,<1.13.1; 1.8.0 sits in the first row.

static_review_summary: Inner::complete calls State::set_complete, which at 1.8.0 is a single fetch_or(VALUE_SENT, AcqRel) (tokio/src/sync/oneshot.rs:854-860). Sender::send stores the value in the Inner UnsafeCell at :310-315 and then calls complete(); if Receiver::close or Receiver::drop has already set CLOSED, set_complete still sets VALUE_SENT, so both sides touch the cell: send sees prev.is_closed(), returns Err and takes the value back through consume_value() (:318-320, value.with_mut(...take()) at :800-801) while a concurrent poll_recv/try_recv that observed VALUE_SENT reads the same cell (:664, :734). Two with_mut accesses from different threads are a data race on the value (CWE-362; memory-corruption class). The fix e0cf906a replaces the fetch_or with a compare-and-swap loop that stops when CLOSED is already set, so VALUE_SENT is never published on a closed channel, and was released in 1.8.4/1.13.1. The pre-image at the frozen tag is identical to the fix hunk and the patch applies with git apply --check.

title: ServerOptions::pipe_mode overwrites dwPipeMode and clears PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS
category_l2: pipe_mode() overwrites dwPipeMode instead of updating the pipe-type bits, dropping the default PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS flag

admission_checks.notes: Frozen tokio-rs/tokio tokio-1.8.0 at 677107d8d9278265798c5efdc75374a25b41a4b8. Named pipes first shipped in 1.7.0, so 1.8.0 is inside the affected window. The real fix is the first commit of PR #5336, 9ca156c0b80347bb7b1406c6050d602f22efc709 ("net: fix named pipes server configuration builder"); the OSV GIT fixed events 9241c3ed and 1a997ffb are the 1.18.4/1.23.1 release-prep commits from the same PR branch. The named_pipe.rs patch applies cleanly to the frozen tree (git apply --check rc=0). Vendor rows are >=1.7.0,<1.18.4, >=1.19.0,<1.20.3 and >=1.21.0,<1.23.1.

static_review_summary: ServerOptions::pipe_mode assigns the whole dwPipeMode DWORD from the selected PipeMode (tokio/src/net/windows/named_pipe.rs:1449-1456), which silently clears PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS. That flag is set by default in ServerOptions::new (:1433) and is manipulated as a bit flag by reject_remote_clients() (:1730-1732), so a server that calls pipe_mode() after configuring, or without configuring, remote-client rejection ends up with dwPipeMode = PIPE_TYPE_BYTE only and accepts remote (SMB) clients, exposing a local IPC endpoint to the network. The fix 9ca156c0b80347bb7b1406c6050d602f22efc709 sets only the 0x4 PIPE_TYPE_MESSAGE bit with bool_flag! so unrelated flags survive, adds unit tests, and was released in 1.18.4/1.20.3/1.23.1. The module is cfg(windows) and not compiled on the Linux checkout, but the source is present at the frozen tag and the patch applies with git apply --check.

title: ReadHalf::unsplit moves T out of an UnsafeCell without requiring T: Unpin
category_l2: ReadHalf::unsplit takes T back out of an UnsafeCell via Arc::try_unwrap without requiring T: Unpin, so a pinned !Unpin stream can be moved

admission_checks.notes: Frozen tokio-rs/tokio tokio-1.8.0 at 677107d8d9278265798c5efdc75374a25b41a4b8. RUSTSEC classifies this as informational/unsound (memory-exposure); the GHSA record rates it low and carries no CVSS vector. The real fix d6ea7a74 ("Add `T: Unpin` bound to ReadHalf::unsplit") was recovered from the tokio-1.18.4...tokio-1.18.5 compare; the split.rs patch applies cleanly to the frozen tree (git apply --check rc=0). Vendor rows are >=0.2.0,<1.18.5, >=1.19.0,<1.20.4 and >=1.21.0,<1.24.2; 1.8.0 sits in the first row.

static_review_summary: ReadHalf::unsplit reunites the halves by Arc::try_unwrap on Inner<T> and then calling UnsafeCell::into_inner on stream (tokio/src/io/split.rs:77-89; Inner is { locked: AtomicBool, stream: UnsafeCell<T> } at :52-55). The halves give out Pin<&mut T> through AsyncRead/AsyncWrite, and at 1.8.0 unsplit had no T: Unpin bound, so a !Unpin stream can be moved out after it has been pinned - a violation of the Pin contract that makes the public API unsound. The fix d6ea7a742b92d3e516035a584ab9347a96be363a adds `where T: Unpin` and was released in 1.18.5/1.20.4/1.24.2. The pre-image is identical to the 1.18.x fix hunk and the patch applies with git apply --check.

title: broadcast channel clones the slot value in parallel with only T: Send
category_l2: slot values are guarded by RwLock read guards, so clone_value can call T::clone concurrently on a T that is only required to be Send, not Sync

admission_checks.notes: Frozen tokio-rs/tokio tokio-1.8.0 at 677107d8d9278265798c5efdc75374a25b41a4b8. The real fix is the code commit of PR #7232, 4b174ce2c95fe1d1a217917db93fcc935e17e0da ("sync: fix cloning value when receiving from broadcast channel"), not the branch tip aa303bc2 (1.38.2 release prep). The 1.38.x patch does not apply wholesale to 1.8.0 because the file gained ~400 lines in the interim. Per-hunk replay: hunk 8 (sender slot write), hunk 13 (receiver slot read) and hunk 15 (Recv::get_unchecked_mut) apply on their own; the rest fail on context/line drift from later 1.x changes. The defect pre-image itself - RwLock read guard + UnsafeCell val + T::clone at :1064 - is byte-identical at the frozen tag, as are the only-T: Send unsafe impls at :468-472. Vendor rows are >=0.2.5,<1.38.2, >=1.39.0,<1.43.1 and >=1.44.0,<1.44.2.

static_review_summary: At 1.8.0 broadcast slots are Box<[RwLock<Slot<T>>]> (tokio/src/sync/broadcast.rs:297-300) holding a bare UnsafeCell<Option<T>> val (:327-346), and RecvGuard::clone_value calls T::clone through the shared read guard (:1060-1065; RecvGuard holds an RwLockReadGuard at :364-365). Because RwLock allows several readers, two receivers can clone the same value concurrently, while the channel only requires T: Send (unsafe impls at :468-472) - a Send-but-not-Sync T whose Clone touches non-atomic interior state is then cloned from two threads at once, which is undefined behaviour (RUSTSEC memory-corruption class). The fix 4b174ce2c95fe1d1a217917db93fcc935e17e0da replaces the RwLock with a Mutex so clones are serialized, stores the value as a plain Option<T>, and drops the manual Send/Sync impls; it was released in 1.38.2/1.43.1/1.44.2. The changed clone_value and drop lines are textually identical at the frozen tag.

title: AsyncFd safe constructors accept any AsRawFd, so an unowned descriptor can be closed or reused while registered
category_l2: safe AsyncFd constructors accept any AsRawFd and register a descriptor they do not own, so the caller can close or reuse it while the driver still holds the registration

admission_checks.notes: Frozen tokio-rs/tokio tokio-1.8.0 at 677107d8d9278265798c5efdc75374a25b41a4b8. RUSTSEC has no CVE or GHSA alias and no CVSS score for this advisory, so it is recorded as T2 with review_status unknown rather than T1. The real fix is the code commit of PR #8587, fb57e675b0dcdd45f251e286b5ddcd96607e1e90 ("io: add `AsyncFd::register` and deprecate `AsyncFd::new`"); the branch merge commit 2598543b8a68 and the release-prep commits are not code fixes. The 1.51.x patch does not apply to 1.8.0 (that branch has try_new, AsyncFdRegisterError and an AsFd impl, none of which exist at 1.8.0); the pre-image of the affected constructors - safe pub fn new(inner: T) with only T: AsRawFd - is present verbatim at :175-180. Vendor rows are >=0.3.2,<1.51.6 and >=1.52.0,<1.53.3; 1.8.0 sits in the first row.

static_review_summary: AsyncFd::new / with_interest are safe functions that accept any T: AsRawFd and never require proof that the descriptor is owned and stays open (tokio/src/io/async_fd.rs:175-196). They cache inner.as_raw_fd() and hand it to Registration::new_with_interest_and_handle (:197-205); since RawFd itself implements AsRawFd, safe code can pass a bare descriptor it later closes or that the process reuses. The io driver packs a pointer to the ScheduledIo slab entry into the mio token when the source is registered (tokio/src/io/driver/mod.rs:320-340) and deregisters by descriptor number through SourceFd, so a caller-supplied descriptor that is closed or reused while the AsyncFd is alive leaves the driver with a stale token and can deregister another resource's descriptor - the I/O-safety violation RUSTSEC describes as leading to use-after-free in the readiness path. The fix fb57e675b0dcdd45f251e286b5ddcd96607e1e90 (PR #8587) makes registration an unsafe fn `register`/`register_with_interest` and deprecates the safe constructors; it was released in 1.51.6/1.53.3/1.54.0. The safe constructor half of the advisory applies at 1.8.0; the AsyncFd: AsFd half does not, because no AsFd impl exists anywhere in the 1.8.0 tree.

title: storeAtts() rescans elementType->defaultAtts for every non-normalized attribute value
category_l2: storeAtts() scans elementType->defaultAtts linearly for every non-normalized attribute value, turning many attributes on one element into quadratic CPU work

admission_checks.notes: Frozen libexpat/libexpat R_2_6_2 at fa75b96546c069d17b8f80d91e0f4ef0cde3790d. OSV records the GIT range introduced 0, last_affected 92810461043f = R_2_8_3 release prep (#1314), and NVD says "through 2.8.3". The fix commit f8f7c4ff is contained in R_2_8_4 (compare R_2_8_4...f8f7c4ff reports ahead_by 0), merged as e97a6c45 on 2026-08-18. The advisory carries no reviewed GHSA; the only CVSS is a Secondary CVSS 4.0 8.7 from vulncheck, so the row is T2/unknown. Fix-diff check: the removed loop at fix-file lines 3967-3974 matches 2.6.2 lines 3453-3461 line for line except `int j` vs `size_t j`; the second hunk (defineAttribute) and the added hash table do not exist at 2.6.2, so git apply --check fails and the pre-image was verified by direct read.

static_review_summary: In storeAtts, every attribute whose value is not already normalized and whose ATTRIBUTE_ID has maybeTokenized set searches elementType->defaultAtts linearly for a matching id to learn whether the attribute was declared as other than CDATA (expat/lib/xmlparse.c:3453-3461).  With N specified attributes and N matching default-attribute declarations that inner scan runs once per attribute, so one element carrying a few hundred thousand attributes costs O(N^2) comparisons and a document of a few megabytes pins a CPU core (CWE-407).  The fix f8f7c4ffd883e3c2c58f0ebb49416a6c1d248738 (PR #1321, merged as e97a6c45 and released in 2.8.4) replaces the scan with a lookup in elementType->defaultAttForName, a hash table keyed by attribute name; the preceding commit 98f5acc1 in the same PR renames that table from defaultAttsNames.  At the frozen 2.6.2 tree the loop is present verbatim except that the loop variable is declared as `int j` (the fix hunk's pre-image uses `size_t j`), and the defaultAttForName/defaultAttsNames table does not exist yet, so the 2.8.x patch does not apply wholesale; the defect site itself matches the fix pre-image.

title: every unmatched opening tag allocates a TAG plus 32-byte buffer with no accounting against input size
category_l2: each unmatched opening tag allocates a TAG and a 32-byte buffer that stay live on the tag stack, with no allocation budget relative to the input size

admission_checks.notes: Frozen libexpat/libexpat R_2_6_2 at fa75b96546c069d17b8f80d91e0f4ef0cde3790d. NVD range is before 2.7.2; the fix merge ac7a27e1 is contained in R_2_7_2 (compare R_2_7_2...ac7a27e1 reports ahead_by 0). OSV's GIT fixed event 7643f96b is "Merge pull request #1038 from libexpat/prepare-release", i.e. release prep, not the code fix; the tracking mechanism is the 19-commit PR #1034. The advisory is an unreviewed NVD/OSV record, so the row is T2/unknown. Static check: the allocation block at :2981-2989 is present verbatim, the free-tag list only recycles tags after end tags (:3090-3098), INIT_TAG_BUF_SIZE is 32 (:260), and sized TAG is 88 bytes with the 2.6.2 struct; there is no allocation accounting in the file before the fix (no MALLOC_TRACKER / expat_malloc). The fix adds tracking in the MALLOC macro, so this site has no textual fix hunk - evidence_type is source_review and the location is the amplification source named in issue #1018, not a patch pre-image.

static_review_summary: doContent allocates a TAG (88 bytes on amd64) plus a separate INIT_TAG_BUF_SIZE buffer (32 bytes, expat/lib/xmlparse.c:260) for every opening tag that is not served from parser->m_freeTagList, and keeps each one on parser->m_tagStack until its end tag is seen (expat/lib/xmlparse.c:2981-2989).  A document made of deeply nested 3-byte tags (`<x>`) therefore pins at least sizeof(TAG)+32 = 120 bytes of dynamic memory per 3 input bytes, and at 2.6.2 nothing accounts for these allocations against the input size.  Upstream issue #1018 measured the effect with EXPAT_ACCOUNTING_DEBUG on a 240 KiB payload: direct 240562 bytes vs 16.7 MB indirect, amplification 70.77, and the existing billion-laughs accounting (which only counts DTD/entity expansion) does not stop it.  The shipped fix, PR #1034 merged as ac7a27e1f034c06e6be590ce98c36db9f8f5eedc and released in 2.7.2, does not change this block: it tracks dynamic allocations in the MALLOC/FREE macros (core commit cfce28e171676fe6f70d17b97ed8a59eaeb83f15) and aborts when tracked allocations pass 64 MiB and exceed 100x the direct input bytes, which caps the amplification that issue #1018 located at this allocation.  The anchor is that allocation site, verified verbatim at the frozen SHA; the evidence is source review, not a fix hunk at the site.

title: derived Debug on the client session value types prints ClientSessionCommon::secret in hex
category_l2: derived Debug for client session values includes ClientSessionCommon::secret, and PayloadU8/Zeroizing Debug print the resumption PSK and master secret as hex

admission_checks.notes: Frozen rustls/rustls v/0.23.4 at 1dee8b13134d877ade94dda7b68c7bf072e18d62. RUSTSEC-2026-0346 gives introduced 0.21.0, fixed 0.23.46, so the frozen tag is affected; the GitHub advisory API renders the range as "< 0.23.46, > 0.24.0-dev.1", which contradicts itself, so the RUSTSEC interval is used. Fix dcdb9464d376f45f42a94a5f837cda1506449f23 ("Eliminate secrets from impl Debug for Tls12Session") is contained in the v/0.23.46 tag (compare v/0.23.46...dcdb9464 -> ahead_by 0); the parallel mainline commit f5f7bf50 touches rustls/src/client/mod.rs, which does not exist at 0.23.4, so it is not the release-branch fix. Static check at the SHA: #[derive(Debug)] on Tls13ClientSessionValue (:71-72) and on Tls12ClientSessionValue (:138), #[derive(Debug, Clone)] on ClientSessionCommon (:204-210) with secret: Zeroizing<PayloadU8> (:207); PayloadU8 Debug prints hex (base.rs:189-193) and zeroize 1.7.0 derives Debug for Zeroizing, so {:?} on a session value prints the secret. Both session types are re-exported publicly at lib.rs:560. The fix regression test asserts !debug.contains("a5a5"). The struct body drifted between 0.23.4 and 0.23.46 (ticket: Arc<PayloadU16>, server_cert_verifier/client_creds fields), so git apply --check fails and the pre-image was verified by direct read. The advisory carries no CVE and no CWE, so cwe_ids is empty and aliases are GHSA + RUSTSEC.; functionless_location: Rust struct definition: the defect is the #[derive(Debug)] attribute on Tls13ClientSessionValue (and on ClientSessionCommon at :204), which has no enclosing function at the anchor

static_review_summary: At v/0.23.4 both public client session types derive Debug (Tls13ClientSessionValue at rustls/src/msgs/persist.rs:71-78 and Tls12ClientSessionValue at :138), and the ClientSessionCommon they embed derives Debug too (:204-210) while holding the resumption secret as `secret: Zeroizing<PayloadU8>` (:207).  PayloadU8 has a manual Debug that hex-dumps its bytes (rustls/src/msgs/base.rs:189-193) and zeroize 1.7.0 derives Debug for Zeroizing, so the derived Debug of a session value prints the TLS 1.3 resumption PSK (or the TLS 1.2 master secret) as hex.  The types are part of the public API - rustls/src/lib.rs:560 re-exports both from rustls::client, and ClientSessionStore returns them - so any application that logs a retrieved session value, or an error payload that contains one, writes the secret to its logs.  The v/0.23.46 fix dcdb9464 removes both derives and hand-writes Debug impls that skip `secret`; its regression test asserts that the formatted value does not contain the 0xa5 secret bytes.

title: an unauthenticated ServerHello stores a per-name KX hint before the handshake is authenticated, pinning the group of later ClientHellos
category_l2: a forged ServerHello saved before authentication pins the single key-exchange group offered in later ClientHellos for that server name

admission_checks.notes: Frozen rustls/rustls v/0.23.4 at 1dee8b13134d877ade94dda7b68c7bf072e18d62. RUSTSEC-2026-0349 records introduced 0.0.0-0, fixed 0.23.46, so the frozen tag is affected. The 0.23-branch fix f04804fa13341a9b1dc02b5d1dd8a746f2c4b7fb ("Delay saving KX hint until handshake confirmation") is the v/0.23.46 tag commit (compare v/0.23.46...f04804fa -> identical); the parallel mainline commit 8fa0dc5d is 1733 commits ahead of 0.23.46 and is not the release-branch fix. The removed block matches tls13.rs:150-154 verbatim (the "Remember what KX group..." comment plus the four set_kx_hint lines); the rest of the patch does not apply because v/0.23.46 contains ECH and handler changes that are absent at 0.23.4, so git apply --check fails and the pre-image was verified by direct read. Static check: the hint is read at :207 by initial_key_share, which starts a single ActiveKeyExchange in that group and falls back to the first configured group only when no hint is stored; at 0.23.4 the provider kx_groups contain no hybrid/PQ entry, so the PQ framing of the advisory does not add impact here, but the unauthenticated hint poisoning does. The advisory carries no CVE and no CWE, so cwe_ids is empty and aliases are GHSA + RUSTSEC.

static_review_summary: handle_server_hello (rustls/src/client/tls13.rs:61) writes the group the server selected into the per-name session store with set_kx_hint (:150-154) immediately after completing the key exchange (:146) and before any certificate or Finished message is verified.  If the handshake later fails - for example a network attacker answers a connection attempt with a ServerHello it cannot authenticate and then drops the connection - the hint survives in the store.  initial_key_share (:200-220) then reads kx_hint (:207) for the same server name and starts exactly one key exchange in that group, so every later ClientHello for that name carries a share only for the attacker-chosen group even though the client supports others.  At v/0.23.4 the configured providers have no hybrid/PQ group, so the advisory's classical-only downgrade scenario cannot be reproduced literally at this tag; the pre-authentication cache-poisoning primitive and its effect on later ClientHellos are nevertheless present.  The v/0.23.46 fix f04804fa removes the early set_kx_hint call, threads kx_group through ExpectEncryptedExtensions and ExpectCertificateOrCompressedCertificateOrCertReq, and writes the hint only in ExpectFinished after the handshake is authenticated.

title: the GIF comment reader treats the EOF byte as a block length, so skipping a malformed comment block never advances
category_l2: an unterminated GIF comment block makes ReadComments consume and rewind at end of stream instead of terminating

admission_checks.notes: Frozen SixLabors/ImageSharp v3.1.6 at 313a7e8daaae0d5eacb50b16b0398e40266e890a. The frozen SHA is the v3.1.6 tag commit (compare v3.1.6...313a7e8d -> identical), and both published ranges ("< 3.1.11" from the GitHub advisory and "3.0.0 through 3.1.10" from the CVE description) contain 3.1.6. The fix f4a2684737732059876c13c481c856ed6b28e2c6 ("Backport V3 - GIF: Check for end of stream when reading comments", merge of PR #2955 for issue #2953) is the v3.1.11 tag commit (compare v3.1.11...f4a26847 -> identical); the mainline commit 833f3cee carries the same five added lines but is 681 commits ahead and 80 behind v3.1.11, so it is not the release-branch fix. The hunk pre-image (the max-length throw plus the blank line before the SkipMetadata branch) matches GifDecoderCore.cs:388-395 verbatim; the hunk header offset differs by 20 lines because 3.1.6 and the fix branch drifted, so the pre-image was verified by direct read rather than git apply --check. The GitHub advisory API reports no cwe_ids, but the CVE/OSV record for CVE-2025-54575 carries CWE-400 and CWE-770, which are used here.

static_review_summary: ReadComments (src/ImageSharp/Formats/Gif/GifDecoderCore.cs:381) drives its loop with `while ((length = stream.ReadByte()) != 0)`, so the -1 that ReadByte returns at end of stream enters the body as a block length.  The only length guard is `length > GifConstants.MaxCommentSubBlockLength`, which -1 passes.  With SkipMetadata set, the body executes `stream.Seek(length, SeekOrigin.Current)` (:396) and rewinds one byte, so a comment extension with a missing terminator keeps the reader bouncing at the end of the stream instead of finishing the block; without SkipMetadata the negative length goes straight into `memoryAllocator.Allocate<byte>(length)` (:399).  A crafted GIF with an unterminated comment block therefore hangs (or faults) any decoder that identifies or loads untrusted input, for example an image service that re-encodes uploads.  The v3.1.11 backport f4a26847 adds an explicit `if (length == -1) throw ... "Unexpected end of stream while reading gif comment"` right after the max-length check, and its regression test asserts InvalidImageContentException for Identify and Load both with and without SkipMetadata.

title: the CCITT T4 encoder writes past an output buffer sized at only one byte per pixel
category_l2: the CCITT T4 encoder emits up to 13 bits per pixel plus EOL codes into a buffer sized for eight bits per pixel

admission_checks.notes: Frozen SixLabors/ImageSharp v3.1.6 at 313a7e8daaae0d5eacb50b16b0398e40266e890a, which is the v3.1.6 tag commit (compare v3.1.6...313a7e8d -> identical). The advisory range ">= 2.0.0, < 3.2.0" contains 3.1.6. The fix baa37cd19077b2a2a0c5667535111cf31d48c019 ("Fix CCITT encoder buffer sizing and bounds", v3.2.0 tag commit, compare v3.2.0...baa37cd1 -> identical) inserts GetMaximumEncodedBits immediately after CompressStrip (T4BitCompressor.cs:126-127 in the pre-image, :39-127 here) and adds the availableBits check at TiffCcittCompressor.cs:466; both pre-image blocks match the frozen file verbatim, but the fix commit also changes unrelated files, so the pre-image was verified by direct read rather than a full git apply --check. Static check at the SHA: Initialize (:529-531) computes maxNeededBytes = Width * rowsPerStrip with no bit budget, WriteCode (:466) has no bounds check, BitWriterUtils.WriteBit (BitWriterUtils.cs:52-55) writes through Unsafe.Add, and T4BitCompressor.CompressStrip calls WriteCode for the initial EOL (:44), each run (:83, :95, :102, :110, :114) and each EOL (WriteEndOfLine :129-141, WriteCode at :138). The 3.x sibling CVEs 106114/106117/106118 were promoted earlier from the same v3.2.0 diff.

static_review_summary: TiffCcittCompressor.Initialize (src/ImageSharp/Formats/Tiff/Compression/Compressors/TiffCcittCompressor.cs:527) sizes the shared output buffer as `int maxNeededBytes = this.Width * rowsPerStrip`, i.e. one byte (eight bits) per pixel, while the Group 3 encoder emits up to a 13-bit terminating code per pixel plus a 12-bit EOL and an 8-bit zero-length white run per row.  T4BitCompressor.CompressStrip (T4BitCompressor.cs:39) then writes through WriteCode (TiffCcittCompressor.cs:466), which advances bytePosition and calls BitWriterUtils.WriteBit; that helper does `Unsafe.Add(ref MemoryMarshal.GetReference(buffer), bufferPos)` with no bounds check, so a bi-level image with alternating pixels (the worst case for the run-length codes) writes past the pooled buffer.  The v3.2.0 fix baa37cd1 adds an abstract GetMaximumEncodedBits, implements it for T4 as `12 + ((Width * 13) + 20) * rowsPerStrip` bits, sizes Initialize from it, and makes WriteCode throw InvalidMemoryOperationException when the remaining bits are insufficient.

title: histogram equalization turns an unclamped float luminance into an unchecked histogram index
category_l2: an unclamped or NaN float luminance becomes an out-of-range index into the histogram equalization accumulator

admission_checks.notes: Frozen SixLabors/ImageSharp v3.1.6 at 313a7e8daaae0d5eacb50b16b0398e40266e890a (v3.1.6 tag commit, compare v3.1.6...313a7e8d -> identical); the advisory range ">= 2.0.0, < 3.2.0" contains it. The fix baa37cd19077b2a2a0c5667535111cf31d48c019 is the v3.2.0 tag commit (compare v3.2.0...baa37cd1 -> identical) and its ColorNumerics.cs hunk pre-image (the single expression-bodied GetBT709Luminance plus the two surrounding doc lines) matches ColorNumerics.cs:27-31 verbatim; the pre-image was verified by direct read because the same commit changes many other files. Static check at the SHA: GetBT709Luminance (:29-30) performs no NaN test and no clamp, GrayscaleLevelsRowOperation.cs:60-61 uses the result as the offset of an Unsafe.Add into the 65536-entry histogram, and HistogramEqualization calls the row operation for every row of the source image. The advisory lists CWE-787 and CVSS 7.5 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H.

static_review_summary: ColorNumerics.GetBT709Luminance (src/ImageSharp/Common/Helpers/ColorNumerics.cs:29) returns `(int)MathF.Round(Vector4.Dot(vector, Bt709) * (luminanceLevels - 1))` without clamping the dot product to [0, 1] or rejecting NaN.  Floating-point pixel formats can hold components outside their normalized range (and operations such as Normalize or convolution can produce NaN), so the rounded value can fall below 0 or above luminanceLevels - 1.  GrayscaleLevelsRowOperation{TPixel} (src/ImageSharp/Processing/Processors/Normalization/GrayscaleLevelsRowOperation{TPixel}.cs:60) passes that value to `Interlocked.Increment(ref Unsafe.Add(ref histogramBase, (uint)luminance))`, an unchecked write into a 65536-entry histogram, so a crafted float image drives the histogram-equalization processor out of the histogram allocation; GlobalHistogramEqualizationProcessor{TPixel}.cs:133 and AutoLevelProcessor{TPixel}.cs:152 make the same call.  The v3.2.0 fix baa37cd1 replaces the expression with a body that returns 0 for NaN and clamps the luminance to [0, 1] before scaling.

title: the CCITT T6 encoder writes past an output buffer sized at only one byte per pixel
category_l2: the CCITT T6 encoder emits up to 16 bits per pixel plus the EOFB into a buffer sized for eight bits per pixel

admission_checks.notes: Frozen SixLabors/ImageSharp v3.1.6 at 313a7e8daaae0d5eacb50b16b0398e40266e890a (v3.1.6 tag commit, compare v3.1.6...313a7e8d -> identical); the advisory range ">= 2.1.0, < 3.2.0" contains it. The fix baa37cd19077b2a2a0c5667535111cf31d48c019 is the v3.2.0 tag commit (compare v3.2.0...baa37cd1 -> identical) and inserts the T6 GetMaximumEncodedBits right after CompressStrip (T6BitCompressor.cs:131-132 in the pre-image, :53-132 here); the pre-image block matches the frozen file verbatim and was verified by direct read because the commit also changes unrelated files. Static check at the SHA: Initialize (:529-531) has no bit budget, WriteCode (:466) has no bounds check, and T6BitCompressor.CompressStrip writes pass codes (:72), horizontal and vertical codes through WriteRun (:184-198) and the two closing EOFB codes (:130-131). The sibling CVE-2026-106110 covers the same sizing defect on the T4 path and is anchored at T4BitCompressor. CompressStrip.

static_review_summary: TiffCcittCompressor.Initialize (src/ImageSharp/Formats/Tiff/Compression/Compressors/TiffCcittCompressor.cs:527) allocates Width * rowsPerStrip bytes for every CCITT strip, but the Group 4 encoder needs up to 16 bits per pixel plus row transition overhead and a final 24-bit EOFB.  T6BitCompressor.CompressStrip (T6BitCompressor.cs:53) emits pass, vertical and horizontal mode codes through WriteCode (TiffCcittCompressor.cs:466), whose bit writes go through BitWriterUtils.WriteBit and an unchecked `Unsafe.Add` on the destination span, so a bi-level image with alternating pixels drives bytePosition past the end of the pooled buffer.  The v3.2.0 fix baa37cd1 adds GetMaximumEncodedBits for T6 as `((Width * 16) + 24) * rowsPerStrip + 24` bits, sizes Initialize from it, and makes WriteCode throw when the remaining bits are insufficient.

title: a BigTIFF entry count that exceeds the directory data drives ReadValues64 through a non-progressing loop
category_l2: a BigTIFF IFD entry count larger than the remaining data makes ReadValues64 iterate without the stream advancing

admission_checks.notes: Frozen SixLabors/ImageSharp v3.1.6 at 313a7e8daaae0d5eacb50b16b0398e40266e890a (v3.1.6 tag commit, compare v3.1.6...313a7e8d -> identical); the advisory range ">= 2.0.0, < 3.2.0" contains it. The fix baa37cd19077b2a2a0c5667535111cf31d48c019 is the v3.2.0 tag commit (compare v3.2.0...baa37cd1 -> identical) and its ExifReader.cs hunk pre-image - Seek, ReadUInt64 count, blank line, stackalloc offsetBuffer and the loop - matches ExifReader.cs:203-210 verbatim; the hunk header sits at line 224 because the fix branch inserted other reader methods before this one, so the pre-image was verified by direct read. Static check at the SHA: ReadValues64 (:199-211) has no upper bound on count, ReadValue64 (:418-423) is the early return when fewer than 20 bytes remain, and neither path advances this.data.Position, so the loop cannot terminate early. The advisory lists CWE-835 and CVSS 5.3 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L.

static_review_summary: ExifReader.ReadValues64 (src/ImageSharp/Metadata/Profiles/Exif/ExifReader.cs:199) seeks to the IFD offset, reads the 64-bit entry count from the file, and loops `for (ulong i = 0; i < count; i++) this.ReadValue64(values, offsetBuffer)`.  ReadValue64 (:418) starts with `if ((this.data.Length - this.data.Position) < 20) return;`, so once fewer than 20 bytes remain it returns without reading anything or advancing the stream position.  A BigTIFF whose first IFD declares a count larger than the remaining data therefore keeps iterating without progress for the full declared count (up to 2^64-1), pinning the decoding thread.  The v3.2.0 fix baa37cd1 bounds the count with the bytes actually available - `remainingDirectoryBytes = data.Length - data.Position` must cover the 8-byte next-IFD offset plus 20 bytes per entry - and throws InvalidImageContentException otherwise.

title: the login POST filter authenticates credentials without a CSRF crumb, so a cross-site form can log the victim into the attacker's account
category_l2: the j_spring_security_check POST is authenticated without a crumb, so a cross-site form logs the victim into the attacker account

admission_checks.notes: Frozen jenkinsci/jenkins jenkins-2.441 at 3b0de10df3bedba515e13032104d4d84f83045be; the frozen SHA is the jenkins-2.441 tag commit (compare jenkins-2.441...3b0de10d -> identical). The advisory covers "Jenkins 2.540 and earlier, LTS 2.528.2 and earlier" and OSV models the 2.441 line as introduced 0, fixed 2.528.3 (the weekly branch is a separate range, 2.529..2.541), so 2.441 is inside the affected range. The fix 31598feb0aa514d8978d2c27a4c9a5a9b8d80a57 ("[SECURITY-1166]") is the 2.541 / 2.528.3 change; its hunk pre-image at the constructor does not apply verbatim because the fix branch has already migrated the request matcher to PathPatternRequestMatcher while 2.441 still constructs `new AntPathRequestMatcher(...)` at :59, so the pre-image was verified by direct read. Static check at the SHA: the class has no attemptAuthentication override (:55-105), SecurityRealm registers the filter for `j_spring_security_check` (:599), and login.jelly (:77-78) plus SetupWizard/authenticate-security-token.jelly submit without a crumb field. The advisory carries CWE-352 and NVD scores it 3.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N).

static_review_summary: AuthenticationProcessingFilter2 (core/src/main/java/hudson/security/AuthenticationProcessingFilter2.java:55) is the Spring Security filter registered for the authentication gateway URL `j_spring_security_check` (SecurityRealm.java:223-228, instantiated at :599).  At 2.441 it extends UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter and overrides only successfulAuthentication (:66) and unsuccessfulAuthentication (:93); it does not override attemptAuthentication, so the POST that carries j_username/j_password is authenticated without any Jenkins crumb validation.  The login form (core/src/main/resources/jenkins/model/Jenkins/login.jelly:77-78) posts only `from`, `j_username` and `j_password`, and the setup wizard token form posts the same way, so neither carries a crumb.  A cross-site form can therefore submit the attacker's credentials to /j_spring_security_check with the victim's browser: the victim is silently logged into the attacker's account (login CSRF), and work the victim performs afterwards is stored in that account.  The fix 31598feb adds an attemptAuthentication override that fetches the CrumbIssuer, reads the crumb from the request parameter or header and throws InsufficientAuthenticationException when it does not validate (with a SKIP_CSRF_CHECK system property as an escape hatch), and adds the hidden `${h.getCrumbRequestField()}` / `${h.getCrumb(request2)}` inputs to login.jelly and SetupWizard/authenticate-security-token.jelly.

title: middleware/proxy bypass in Pages Router i18n applications: the default locale is not prefixed onto /_next/data
category_l2: middleware path matcher sees a locale-less /_next/data path

admission_checks.notes: Frozen vercel/next.js v14.2.24 at 756be15c4cfecb6fae1c69cae7cfaf336423b6cf; the frozen SHA is the v14.2.24 tag commit (compare v14.2.24...756be15c -> identical). Fix 6c72e0b4ee is the release fix; the hunk pre-image was verified by direct read of the frozen file.

static_review_summary: In getResolveRoutes (packages/next/src/server/lib/router-utils/resolve-routes.ts:399-407) the i18n handling for a normal request prepends the default locale (lines 198-210), but for a /_next/data request it only records `__nextLocale` from normalizeLocalePath and never inserts the default locale into the path. The middleware therefore receives a different pathname than the one the page router resolves, so a middleware/proxy matcher can be bypassed by requesting the data route directly. The fix 6c72e0b4ee normalizes the data-route path with the same locale prefixing as a page request.

title: middleware/proxy redirect responses can be cache-poisoned because x-nextjs-data and x-next-resume-state-length are not stripped
category_l2: internal header filter misses two request headers used by the data route

admission_checks.notes: Frozen vercel/next.js v14.2.24 at 756be15c4cfecb6fae1c69cae7cfaf336423b6cf; the frozen SHA is the v14.2.24 tag commit (compare v14.2.24...756be15c -> identical). Fix ac51823b5b is the release fix; the hunk pre-image was verified by direct read of the frozen file.; functionless_location: module-level INTERNAL_HEADERS array; the file has no function that contains the list

static_review_summary: The INTERNAL_HEADERS list in packages/next/src/server/lib/server-ipc/utils.ts:42-51 has eight entries but omits `x-nextjs-data` and `x-next-resume-state-length`.  Those headers are therefore passed through from an untrusted request into the internal render/redirect path, where a middleware redirect can be turned into a response that a shared cache stores under the attacker's URL.  The fix ac51823b5b adds the two names to the internal-header filter.

title: cross-site scripting in beforeInteractive scripts built with JSON.stringify inside an inline push() call
category_l2: JSON.stringify does not escape "<" before the props are inlined into a script tag

admission_checks.notes: Frozen vercel/next.js v14.2.24 at 756be15c4cfecb6fae1c69cae7cfaf336423b6cf; the frozen SHA is the v14.2.24 tag commit (compare v14.2.24...756be15c -> identical). Fix 086dfa7f8f is the release fix; the hunk pre-image was verified by direct read of the frozen file.

static_review_summary: Script (packages/next/src/client/script.tsx:340-344) serializes the props of a beforeInteractive script with JSON.stringify and interpolates the result into `(self.__next_s=self.__next_s||[]).push(...)` with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.  JSON.stringify escapes quotes but not `<`, so a `</script>` sequence in an untrusted prop closes the inline script element and executes attacker markup.  The fix 086dfa7f8f escapes `<` to `\u003c` (and the same for the second push site) before embedding.

admission_checks.notes: Frozen vercel/next.js v14.2.24 at 756be15c4cfecb6fae1c69cae7cfaf336423b6cf; the frozen SHA is the v14.2.24 tag commit (compare v14.2.24...756be15c -> identical). Fix 79d7dff144 is the release fix; the hunk pre-image was verified by direct read of the frozen file.

static_review_summary: getScriptNonceFromHeader (packages/next/src/server/app-render/get-script-nonce-from-header.tsx:43-50) accepts a nonce from the Content-Security-Policy request header unless it matches ESCAPE_REGEX `/[&><\u2028\u2029]/g`; `"` is not in that class, so a nonce containing a quote survives and is interpolated into the response CSP header and script tags, breaking out of the attribute.  The fix 79d7dff144 rejects the nonce when ESCAPE_REGEX matches and also strips a leading quote.

title: server-side request forgery through WebSocket upgrade requests that carry an absolute URL
category_l2: upgrade request absolute URL is proxied to an attacker host

admission_checks.notes: Frozen vercel/next.js v14.2.24 at 756be15c4cfecb6fae1c69cae7cfaf336423b6cf; the frozen SHA is the v14.2.24 tag commit (compare v14.2.24...756be15c -> identical). Fix c4f69086cc is the release fix; the hunk pre-image was verified by direct read of the frozen file.

static_review_summary: The upgrade handler in initialize (packages/next/src/server/lib/router-server.ts:699-700) proxies every request whose parsed URL has a protocol, including the URL taken from an upgrade request line.  An attacker that opens a WebSocket upgrade with an absolute `ws://`/`http://` URL makes the Next.js server issue the proxied request to that host.  The fix c4f69086cc restricts proxying to the configured host/basePath and rejects absolute URLs on the upgrade path.

title: denial of service in the Image Optimization API: internal image responses are buffered without a size limit
category_l2: unbounded Buffer.concat of the internal image response

admission_checks.notes: Frozen vercel/next.js v14.2.24 at 756be15c4cfecb6fae1c69cae7cfaf336423b6cf; the frozen SHA is the v14.2.24 tag commit (compare v14.2.24...756be15c -> identical). Fix 3f1b7b7501 is the release fix; the hunk pre-image was verified by direct read of the frozen file.

static_review_summary: fetchInternalImage (packages/next/src/server/image-optimizer.ts:612) concatenates every buffered chunk of the internal image response into one Buffer with no length cap, and the surrounding call path has no readableLimit.  An attacker can point the image optimizer at a local route that streams an arbitrarily large body and exhaust server memory.  The fix 3f1b7b7501 enforces a maximum upstream body size before buffering.

title: denial of service through remotePatterns: external image responses are buffered without a size limit
category_l2: unbounded arrayBuffer() of a remotePatterns image response

admission_checks.notes: Frozen vercel/next.js v14.2.24 at 756be15c4cfecb6fae1c69cae7cfaf336423b6cf; the frozen SHA is the v14.2.24 tag commit (compare v14.2.24...756be15c -> identical). Fix 39a2f6a8d1 is the release fix; the hunk pre-image was verified by direct read of the frozen file.

static_review_summary: fetchExternalImage (packages/next/src/server/image-optimizer.ts:576) reads the entire upstream response with `res.arrayBuffer()` before any size check, so a remote host allowed by a broad remotePatterns entry can return a multi-gigabyte body and exhaust the server.  The 15.x fix 39a2f6a8d1 caps the upstream body size and rejects oversized responses for both the internal and external paths.

title: unauthenticated remote code execution on Windows hosts through path traversal in the file-system incremental cache
category_l2: cache key path join without containment; backslash not escaped on Windows

admission_checks.notes: Frozen vercel/next.js v14.2.24 at 756be15c4cfecb6fae1c69cae7cfaf336423b6cf; the frozen SHA is the v14.2.24 tag commit (compare v14.2.24...756be15c -> identical). Fix b0f3460a92 is the release fix; the hunk pre-image was verified by direct read of the frozen file.

static_review_summary: getFilePath (packages/next/src/server/lib/incremental-cache/file-system-cache.ts:442-461) builds the on-disk path with `path.join(this.serverDistDir, kind, pathname)` without checking that the resolved path stays under the cache directory, and escapePathDelimiters only rewrites `/`, `#`, `?` and their percent-encodings, not `\`.  On Windows a cache key containing `..\..\` therefore escapes the cache directory and lets an unauthenticated requester write attacker-controlled cache files, which the fix advisory ties to code execution.  The fix b0f3460a92 adds a path-containment check and treats `\` as a delimiter (second fix 968b9fcb26 backports it to 15.5.x).

title: cache poisoning through collisions in the RSC cache-busting query: a 32-bit djb2 hash truncated to five base36 characters
category_l2: five-character truncated djb2 cache-busting key allows collisions

admission_checks.notes: Frozen vercel/next.js v14.2.24 at 756be15c4cfecb6fae1c69cae7cfaf336423b6cf; the frozen SHA is the v14.2.24 tag commit (compare v14.2.24...756be15c -> identical). Fix 8c96fec056 is the release fix; the hunk pre-image was verified by direct read of the frozen file.

static_review_summary: fetchServerResponse (packages/next/src/client/components/router-reducer/fetch-server-response.ts:87-93) derives the `_rsc` cache-busting parameter from `hexHash([...].join(","))`, and hexHash (packages/next/src/shared/lib/hash.ts:17-19) is djb2 reduced to 32 bits and then `toString(36).slice(0, 5)`.
