admission_checks.notes: Frozen symfony/symfony v5.4.45 at 2b66d7d7d8129531229708ef708860844db91944 (HttpKernel Kernel::VERSION '5.4.45'); the cached source tree is the v5.4.45 tag checkout, so every anchor line and the fix pre-image were read verbatim at the frozen file. Fix pre-image at the frozen SHA: the Windows branch starts at :1641 with `if (!preg_match('/[\\/()%!^"<>&|\\s]/', $argument))`, i.e. the class lacks exactly the characters the fix adds (5.4.51 line: '/[()%!^"<>&|\s[\]=;*?\'$]/'). The function spans :1630-1647. Severity is GHSA/NVD CVSS 3.1 6.3 MEDIUM (AV:L/AC:H/UI:R, Windows-only path); no independent re-scoring.

static_review_summary: Process::escapeArgument at src/Symfony/Component/Process/Process.php:1630-1647 has a Windows-only branch that returns the argument unquoted when it does not match /[\/()%!^"<>&|\s]/ (:1641). The class omits "=", ";", "*", "?", "'", "$", "[" and "]", which MSYS2 treats as special when PHP itself runs under an MSYS2 environment (Git Bash) and spawns a native Windows executable: the MSYS2 argument/path conversion mangles the unquoted value, so the child receives a corrupted or truncated argument instead of the one Symfony intended (CWE-88). Applications (or Composer scripts) that pass an attacker-influenced path containing "=" to file-management commands such as rmdir/del can therefore act on a broader directory. The fix ec154f6/3520393 replaces the class with /[()%!^"<>&|\s[\]=;*?\'$]/, forcing the quoting branch for these characters; it is released on 5.4 in 5.4.51.

title: Mime ParameterizedHeader emits parameter names verbatim, so a CRLF or non-token name injects extra mail headers
category_l2: header injection: parameter names are not checked against the RFC token grammar and are emitted verbatim, so CRLF or tspecials in a name inject headers into structured MIME headers
affected_range: >=0, <5.4.55 on the 5.4 line (FriendsOfPHP symfony/mime CVE-2026-45070.yaml, 2026-10-28; GHSA-vqc8-7275-q272 states 5.4.52 but that tag has no name check; the 5.4.55 backport 1503ceb adds it); other lines fixed 6.4.40/7.4.12/8.0.12; v5.4.45 is inside

admission_checks.notes: Frozen symfony/symfony v5.4.45 at 2b66d7d7d8129531229708ef708860844db91944 (HttpKernel Kernel::VERSION '5.4.45'); the cached source tree is the v5.4.45 tag checkout, so every anchor line and the fix pre-image were read verbatim at the frozen file. Fix pre-image at the frozen SHA: setParameters is exactly `public function setParameters(array $parameters) { $this->parameters = $parameters; }` at :57-60, and the only TOKEN_REGEX checks in the file are against $value at :117 and :178. The GHSA carries no CVSS; NVD publishes CVSS 4.0 6.3 MEDIUM and CVSS 3.1 6.5 MEDIUM, and the 3.1 score is stored here. v5.4.52 was diffed against the frozen file for this review and is identical, so the GHSA fixed version is stale.

static_review_summary: ParameterizedHeader::setParameters at src/Symfony/Component/Mime/Header/ParameterizedHeader.php:57-60 stores the caller-supplied parameter array without validating the names, and createParameter (:107) interpolates $name into the serialized header (`$name."=".$value`) after checking only the value against TOKEN_REGEX (:117). RFC 2045/5322 require parameter names to be tokens; a caller that derives a name from untrusted input can therefore put CR/LF or other non-token bytes into Content-Type/Content-Disposition and inject additional headers into the rendered mail (CWE-93). The fix 8cc149f/1503ceb adds a per-name preg_match(TOKEN_REGEX) in setParameters that throws RfcComplianceException. Note on versions: the GHSA record states fixed 5.4.52, but v5.4.52's ParameterizedHeader.php is byte-identical to v5.4.45 and the name check first appears in the 5.4.55 backport 1503ceb (2026-10-28, matching FriendsOfPHP symfony/mime CVE-2026-45070.yaml, affected <5.4.55); v5.4.45 is inside either range.

title: FormDataReader.ProcessFormKeys() loops forever on a form key whose "[" has no matching "]", hanging the request thread
category_l2: ProcessFormKeys adds startIndex to IndexOf(']') before testing for -1, so a form key whose "[" is not at index 0 and has no closing "]" never advances startIndex and loops forever
affected_range: >=8.0.0, <8.0.27 (GHSA-9v76-4qcc-frgh 8.0 range; the same advisory fixes 9.0 <9.0.16 and 10.0 <10.0.8); fixed by ab7d766648 in the v8.0.27 servicing tag and #66674 on main; v8.0.13 is inside

admission_checks.notes: Frozen dotnet/aspnetcore v8.0.13 at 009e1ccafde4086ea52999e878f6e7aa5a7c4ccf; the cached source tree is the v8.0.13 tag checkout (eng/Version.Details.xml pins Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref 8.0.13), so the anchor function and the fix pre-image were read verbatim at the frozen file. Fix pre-image at the frozen SHA: ProcessFormKeys spans :124-165 and contains exactly the code the fix deletes, including `:140 var endIndex = key.Value.Span[startIndex..].IndexOf(']') + startIndex;` and the resume line `:160 startIndex = nextOpenBracket != -1 ? endIndex + 1 + nextOpenBracket : -1;`. The fix ab7d766648 ("Merged PR 59459: [Form binding] Fix parsing of malformed keys (net 8.0)", 2026-04-14) and its public main backport #66674 describe the same off-by-one and are the only infinite-loop fix in the v8.0.27 range; the advisory (CWE-835, AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N, A:H) was published 2026-05-12 for the 8.0.27/9.0.16/10.0.8 servicing release. Severity is the advisory CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH; no independent re-scoring.

static_review_summary: FormDataReader.ProcessFormKeys at src/Components/Endpoints/src/FormMapping/FormDataReader.cs:124-165 splits each form key into bracket segments. It computes `endIndex = key.Value.Span[startIndex..].IndexOf(']') + startIndex` (:140) and then tests `endIndex == -1` (:141), but adding startIndex first turns the -1 sentinel into startIndex-1, so the guard can only fire when the "[" is at index 0. For an ordinary key such as "customer[0" (no closing bracket anywhere after the "[" at index 8) endIndex becomes 7, the code slices an empty key segment, then resumes at `endIndex + 1 + nextOpenBracket` where the "[" search starts at endIndex+1 == startIndex and finds the same "[" again (:158-160): startIndex never advances and the while loop runs forever, pinning the request thread with no further allocation (CWE-835). The reader is driven by form binding for Razor Components and by minimal-API [FromForm] binding (the same fix also touches RequestDelegateFactory.cs and HttpContextFormValueMapper.cs), so any endpoint that accepts form data is reachable by an unauthenticated POST whose field name contains an unmatched "[" (e.g. `customer[0`). The 8.0.27 fix ab7d766648 (public backport #66674, merge b48ed8d3) deletes ProcessFormKeys and rewrites GetKeys() to check `key.Span[prefix.Length] != '['` and to skip a key with no closing "]" via `continue`, so no loop remains.

title: Pure-Python message decoder has no recursion counter, so nested messages, groups and SGROUP tags exhaust the Python stack
category_l2: MessageDecoder and InternalParse call the recursive parser with no depth parameter, so nested messages, recursive groups and SGROUP tag chains exhaust the CPython recursion limit
affected_range: >=4.25.0, <4.25.8 on the 4.25 line (NVD CPE google:protobuf-python versionEndExcluding 4.25.8, plus 5.26.0-<5.29.5 and 6.30.0-<6.31.1; GHSA-8qvm-5x2c-j2w7 lists <4.25.8, <5.29.5, <6.31.1); fixed by 17838b on main and the 25.x backport d31100c9 released as protobuf-python 4.25.8; the frozen python is 4.25.4

admission_checks.notes: Frozen protocolbuffers/protobuf tag v3.25.4 at e915ce24 (v4.25.4 peels to the same commit; version.json lists python 4.25.4 and python/google/protobuf/__init__.py sets __version__ = 4.25.4). The cached tree is the tag checkout, so the anchor was read verbatim at the frozen SHA and the patched construct compared against the fetched release file. Fix pre-image at the frozen SHA: MessageDecoder spans :661-708 and its closures call `value.add()._InternalParse(buffer, pos, new_pos)` (:682) and `value._InternalParse(buffer, pos, new_pos)` (:703); python_message.py:1139 is `def InternalParse(self, buffer, pos, end):` and calls field_decoder(...) at :1164/:1198 without a depth argument; grep for current_depth/_recursion_limit in the frozen decoder.py finds nothing, while the fetched v4.25.8 file has them at the same call sites. The advisory covers groups and SGROUP chains as well: the same backport threads current_depth through _DecodeUnknownField/_DecodeUnknownFieldSet (:945/:962 here) and adds python/google/protobuf/internal/self_recursive.proto plus TestRecursiveGroup in message_test.py (_MakeRecursiveGroupMessage(100) parses, 300 raises "Error parsing message: too many levels of nesting") and test_decode_unknown_group_field_too_many_levels in decoder_test.py. Main fix 17838b ("Add recursion depth limits to pure python") introduces DEFAULT_RECURSION_LIMIT = 100 and SetRecursionLimit. Severity: NVD CVSS 3.1 5.3 MEDIUM; the Google CNA CVSS 4.0 score is 8.2 and is recorded here only as a note.

static_review_summary: In the pure-Python backend, MessageDecoder at python/google/protobuf/internal/decoder.py:661-708 generates the message-field decoders DecodeRepeatedField (:671) and DecodeField (:693); both call `value._InternalParse(buffer, pos, new_pos)` (:682 and :703) with no depth argument, and InternalParse (python_message.py:1139) itself calls every field decoder as `field_decoder(buffer, new_pos, end, self, field_dict)` with no depth. Nothing in the parser counts nesting levels, so a message containing recursively nested sub-messages recurses once per level until CPython raises RecursionError; the equivalent group paths (_DecodeUnknownFieldSet/_DecodeUnknownField at decoder.py:945/962, reached through InternalParse :1182) and chains of SGROUP tags recurse the same way (CWE-674). Any application that parses untrusted protobuf data with PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python (or the pure-Python wheel/Bazel default) can be crashed remotely. The main fix 17838b adds a DEFAULT_RECURSION_LIMIT=100 plus SetRecursionLimit and increments/checks current_depth around every recursive parse; the 25.x backport d31100c9 threads the same current_depth parameter through InternalParse and the decoder closures and ships as protobuf-python 4.25.8.

title: json_format._ConvertAnyMessage skips ConvertMessage for well-known-type Any payloads, so nested Any messages bypass max_recursion_depth
category_l2: _ConvertAnyMessage calls the WKT converter directly instead of ConvertMessage, so the recursion_depth increment that enforces max_recursion_depth is skipped for Any payloads of well-known types
affected_range: < 5.29.6 and 6.30.0rc1-6.33.4 (GHSA-7gcm-g887-7qv7; fixed in 5.29.6 and 6.33.5; the second range is >= 6.30.0rc1, <= 6.33.4); fixed by d2b00162 on main and 5ebddcb1 on 5.x; the frozen python 4.25.4 is below 5.29.6

admission_checks.notes: Frozen protocolbuffers/protobuf tag v3.25.4 at e915ce24 (v4.25.4 peels to the same commit; version.json lists python 4.25.4 and python/google/protobuf/__init__.py sets __version__ = 4.25.4). The cached tree is the tag checkout, so the anchor was read verbatim at the frozen SHA and the patched construct compared against the fetched release file. Fix pre-image at the frozen SHA: _ConvertAnyMessage spans :626-656 and the WKT branch at :646-649 is exactly the methodcaller call the fix replaces; ConvertMessage at :463 increments `self.recursion_depth` at :474 and tests it at :475-477, and ParseDict defaults to max_recursion_depth=100 (:396). The neighbouring _IsWrapperMessage branch (:643-645) also calls a converter directly, but wrapper payloads are scalars and do not recurse, so the fix (d2b00162, PR #25239, "Fix Any recursion depth bypass in Python json_format.ParseDict") leaves it untouched and only routes the _WKTJSONMETHODS branch, which can hold a nested Any, through ConvertMessage. Severity: NVD CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH (CVSS 4.0 8.2 from the Google CNA is recorded as a note). The GHSA page (global advisory record) is the only advisory source; the repository advisory endpoint returns 404 for this ID, so the advisory URL is the canonical GHSA page.

static_review_summary: json_format._ConvertAnyMessage at python/google/protobuf/json_format.py:626-656 parses an Any. ConvertMessage (:463) is the only place that increments self.recursion_depth and raises when it exceeds self.max_recursion_depth (:474-477), but when the Any payload type is a well-known type the code calls the WKT method directly through `methodcaller(_WKTJSONMETHODS[full_name][1], value['value'], sub_message, path)(self)` (:646-649) instead of self.ConvertMessage, so that nesting level is never counted. An attacker-supplied JSON document with deeply nested Any messages can therefore pass the intended depth guard and exhaust the Python stack (CWE-674). ParseDict is the exposed entry point (google.protobuf.json_format.ParseDict, max_recursion_depth=100 by default), so any service that converts untrusted JSON into protobuf messages can be crashed remotely. The fix replaces the methodcaller branch with `self.ConvertMessage(value['value'], sub_message, '{0}.value'.format(path))` (d2b00162 on main, 5ebddcb1 on 5.x) and documents the exclusive depth semantics.

title: PHPMailer executes a language file from an untrusted UNC path in setLanguage() on Windows
category_l2: include of a caller-controlled language path in setLanguage: isPermittedPath only rejects URI schemes, so a UNC path passes, file_exists() performs SMB access and include executes the remote phpmailer.lang-xx.php
affected_range: < 6.5.0 (GHSA-7q44-r25x-wm4q composers range "< 6.5.0" with first_patched_version 6.5.0; NVD CPE cpe:2.3:a:phpmailer_project:phpmailer:* with versionEndExcluding 6.5.0); Windows is named in the advisory title and description; frozen VERSION 6.1.5 is inside

admission_checks.notes: Frozen PHPMailer/PHPMailer v6.1.5 at a8bf068f64a580302026e484ee29511f661b2ad3: tag v6.1.5 is annotated (object 68813f28) and peels to that commit, VERSION reads 6.1.5, and the anchor region was read verbatim at the frozen file. Fix pre-image at the frozen SHA: setLanguage spans :2078-2143; the guard at :2132 is `if (!static::isPermittedPath($lang_file) || !file_exists($lang_file))` and the sink at :2137 is `$foundlang = include $lang_file;`; isPermittedPath (:1745-1748) only rejects `#^[a-z]+://#i`. The fix acd264bf (2021-06-16) is an ancestor of tag v6.5.0 (compare acd264bf...v6.5.0: ahead_by 4, behind_by 0) and is absent from the frozen tree. Severity is NVD Primary CVSS 3.1 8.1 HIGH (nvd@nist.gov, CWE-434 Primary); the GitHub global advisory GHSA-7q44-r25x-wm4q carries the same 8.1 vector and also lists CWE-94, while the maintainers' repository advisory for the same GHSA scored 5.5 MEDIUM (AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:L) on the assumption that the attacker already controls an application setting; the NVD/high figure is recorded.

static_review_summary: PHPMailer::setLanguage at src/PHPMailer.php:2078-2143 assembles `$lang_file = $lang_path . 'phpmailer.lang-' . $langcode . '.php';` (:2128) from the caller-supplied $lang_path and then executes it with `$foundlang = include $lang_file;` (:2137). The sole guard is `if (!static::isPermittedPath($lang_file) || !file_exists($lang_file))` (:2132), where isPermittedPath (:1745-1748) is just `return !preg_match('#^[a-z]+://#i', $path);`. A Windows UNC path such as `\\attacker\share\` contains no URI scheme and passes the check, so file_exists() issues an SMB request to the attacker host and the remote `phpmailer.lang-xx.php` is then included as PHP: RCE on Windows whenever the application passes untrusted data as $lang_path (the advisory precondition), plus NTLM credential disclosure to that share during file_exists(). $langcode itself is constrained by `/^[a-z]{2}(?:_[a-zA-Z]{2})?$/` (:2124), so only the directory component is attacker-defined. The 6.5.0 fix acd264bf ("Merge branch 'CVE-2021-34551'", 2021-06-16) adds the docblock warning "Do not set this from user input!" and replaces the include with `$lines = file($lang_file);` plus a per-line `preg_match('/^\$PHPMAILER_LANG\[\'([a-z\d_]+)\'\]\s*=\s*(["\'])(.+)*?\2;/')` that copies only string assignments for keys already present in the built-in table, so language files are parsed as text and never executed. The frozen 6.1.5 tree still carries the include and the URL-scheme-only check.

title: tinyxml2 aborts on a long numeric character reference because GetCharacterRef bounds mult only with debug assertions
category_l2: numeric character reference parsing keeps `mult`/`ucs` unchecked and relies on TIXMLASSERT, so 8 hex or 10 decimal digits abort assertion-enabled builds while parsing untrusted XML
affected_range: <= 10.0.0 (NVD CPE cpe:2.3:a:tinyxml2_project:tinyxml2:* with versionEndIncluding 10.0.0; OSV GIT range introduced 0, last_affected 321ea883 = tag 10.0.0); fixed in 10.1.0 (494735de, ancestor of tag 10.1.0); frozen 10.0.0 is in range

admission_checks.notes: Frozen leethomason/tinyxml2 10.0.0 at 321ea883b7190d4e85cae5512a12e5eaa8f8731f (tag 10.0.0 resolves to that commit; meson.build project version 10.0.0). Anchor and pre-image were read verbatim at the frozen file. Fix pre-image at the frozen SHA: GetCharacterRef spans :475-568; the hex branch carries `:519 TIXMLASSERT( digit < 16 );`, `:520 TIXMLASSERT( digit == 0 || mult <= UINT_MAX / digit );`, `:521 const unsigned int digitScaled = mult * digit;`, `:522 TIXMLASSERT( ucs <= ULONG_MAX - digitScaled );`, `:523 ucs += digitScaled;` and `:524 TIXMLASSERT( mult <= UINT_MAX / 16 );` before `:525 mult *= 16;`, with the decimal mirrors at :549-559; there is no MAX_CODE_POINT and no ucs upper-bound check anywhere in the frozen GetCharacterRef. The caller StrPair::GetStr allocates `const int buflen = 10; char buf[buflen]` (:329-330) and calls GetCharacterRef at :332. Fix 494735de (2024-12-05) is an ancestor of tag 10.1.0 (compare 494735de...10.1.0: ahead_by 9, behind_by 0); merge 4cbb2515 (2024-12-10, PR #1009) carries the same change. Severity: NVD has no Primary CVSS for this CVE; the only metric is the Secondary CNA metric 6.5 MEDIUM (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) from 134c704f-9b21-4f2e-91b3-4a467353bcc0 (GitHub/MITRE), identical to the global GHSA-xpm9-95h9-q996 record, which is cited in the notes; CWE-617 is the CNA mapping. build_scoping: the abort requires TINYXML2_DEBUG, so this is a debug-configuration DoS; in release builds the unsigned wrap is defined and ConvertUTF32ToUTF8 returns length 0 for input >= 0x200000 (:440-443), which is recorded as a static fact rather than a second impact.

static_review_summary: XMLUtil::GetCharacterRef at tinyxml2.cpp:475-568 parses numeric character references with no upper bound on the number of digits: `unsigned long ucs` and `unsigned mult` (:481, :484) accumulate `ucs += mult * digit; mult *= 16;` (:521-525) in the hex branch and `ucs += digitScaled; mult *= 10;` (:551-559) in the decimal branch. The only guards are the debug assertions `TIXMLASSERT( mult <= UINT_MAX / digit )` (:520), `TIXMLASSERT( ucs <= ULONG_MAX - digitScaled )` (:522) and `TIXMLASSERT( mult <= UINT_MAX / 16 )` (:524), mirrored at (:550, :552, :558) for decimal. TIXMLASSERT expands to `assert` only when TINYXML2_DEBUG is defined (tinyxml2.h:79-93; meson.build:40-42 adds -DTINYXML2_DEBUG for debug builds, CMakeLists.txt:31 for the Debug configuration) and to a no-op otherwise, so in an assertion-enabled build the check aborts the process through __assert_fail as soon as `mult` passes UINT_MAX/16 = 268435455: the hex branch reaches 16^7 = 268435456 after eight digits (e.g. `&#xffffffff;`) and decimal reaches 10^9 after ten digits. The path is reachable from any attribute value or text node through StrPair::GetStr (:322-344), which calls GetCharacterRef for every `&#` entity when entity processing is on (the default), so a document alone can terminate a host that parses untrusted XML -- a DoS in CWE-617 terms, and in non-assertion builds merely a wrapped accumulation that ConvertUTF32ToUTF8 rejects as length 0 (:440-443) or mis-decodes. The 10.1.0 fix 494735de ("fix the potential overflow in char refs", 2024-12-05, merged as 4cbb2515 "Merge pull request #1009") switches the arithmetic to `uint32_t`, defines `MAX_CODE_POINT = 0x10FFFF` and returns 0 as soon as `ucs > MAX_CODE_POINT`, deleting the overflow assertions and adding those inputs (`&#xffffffff;`, `&#5000000000;`, long zero-padded forms) to xmltest.cpp. Frozen 10.0.0 still contains the assertions and no MAX_CODE_POINT; the maintainer confirmed "Should be fixed" on issue #996 on 2026-05-24.

title: libcurl reuses an SMB connection across shares, so a transfer can read or write the wrong share
category_l2: connection reuse matching has no notion of the SMB share: the conncache key is host+port, the per-connection filter compares TLS/proxy/credentials only, and reuse_conn discards the share parsed for the new URL, so the second transfer runs against the first share (read of the wrong file, write into the wrong place)
affected_range: curl 7.40.0 through 8.19.0 (vendor advisory CURL-CVE-2026-5773); backports 8.16.1 in the 8.16.X branch and 8.14.2 in the 8.14.X branch; 8.20.0 disables SMB reuse. Frozen 8.3.0 is below both backport branches and inside the range

admission_checks.notes: Frozen curl/curl curl-8_3_0 at 6fa1d817e5b1a00d7d0c8168091877476b499317: tag curl-8_3_0 is annotated (object 8c537ee3) and peels to that commit; the anchor and pre-image were read verbatim in the cached tree. Anchor at the frozen SHA: ConnectionExists spans lib/url.c:1055-1491 (`static bool` :1055, signature :1056, return :1490, closing brace :1491); the reuse loop runs :1123-1491 and the comparisons at :1190-1298 contain no path/share test. Frozen supporting facts: hashkey builds `%u/%ld/%s` from scope_id, port and hostname (lib/conncache.c:144) and Curl_conncache_find_bundle picks by that key (:167-180); smb.c keeps connections alive (:461) and parses `smbc->share` (:1176); reuse_conn frees the temporary conn (:3354). Fix ancestry: 74a169575d is an ancestor of tag curl-8_20_0 (compare ahead_by 184, behind_by 0) and its diff removes `PROTOPT_CONN_REUSE` from the SMB/SMBS scheme entries; neither the flag nor lib/protocol.c exists at 8.3.0, so this row is recorded with evidence type source_review rather than fix_diff_comparison. Severity: vendor advisory labels the issue Low and publishes no CVSS; NVD has no record for this CVE in this dataset run, so level is low with no score/vector.

static_review_summary: Connection reuse is decided by ConnectionExists (lib/url.c:1055-1491). It first looks up the conncache bundle, whose key is built by hashkey (lib/conncache.c:125-148) as `scope_id/port/hostname` (or `port/hostname`), so it carries no scheme and no URL path; the per-connection filter then compares TLS flags (:1190-1196), proxy settings (:1198-1241), connect-to bits (:1208-1216), local bind (:1269-1286), credentials (:1288-1298) and further transport properties, but never the SMB share. The share is per-URL: smb_setup_connection (:428-440) calls smb_parse_url_path (:1161-1190), which copies the first path component into `smbc->share` (:1176), and the tree connect thereafter names that share (smb_send_tree_connect, :686-698, invoked from smb_request_state :961). SMB marks the connection as reusable (`connkeep(conn, "SMB default")`, :461), so two requests to smb://host/shareA/... and smb://host/shareB/... with the same credentials are matched by ConnectionExists. When the match is taken, reuse_conn (lib/url.c:3286-3355) copies the new credentials/host into the existing connection and then frees the temporary connection (:3354), which discards the smbc parsed for the new URL; the transfer keeps `existing->proto.smbc.share`, so the new request tree-connects to the previous share. The result is a read of a file from the wrong share or a write into the wrong share on the same server with the same credentials (CWE-488). The fix 74a169575d ("protocol: disable connection reuse for SMB(S)", 2026-04-07) removes PROTOPT_CONN_REUSE from the SMB and SMBS rows of the scheme table in lib/protocol.c, i.e. it disables reuse outright instead of matching the share; that table and flag do not exist at 8.3.0 (both handlers there already carry PROTOPT_NONE, lib/smb.c:275 and :303), so the fix has no pre-image in the frozen tree and the anchor is a direct source review of the reuse path.

title: libssh reports a known_hosts key-type mismatch to the SSH key callback as a missing key, so the callback may accept it

The callback is invoked at :513-517 and its FINE/FINE_ADD_TO_FILE arms are :519-535; the no-callback path rejects anything but OK at :537-541. Fix ancestry: 0b8dbbc63 is an ancestor of tag curl-8_21_0 (compare ahead_by 337, behind_by 0); the 8.20.1 backport is a release version, not a git tag. Severity: vendor advisory labels the issue Low and publishes no CVSS; level low with no score/vector.

static_review_summary: myssh_is_known (lib/vssh/libssh.c:334-561) asks libssh for the known_hosts entry (ssh_session_get_known_hosts_entry, :401) and maps the result to a CURLKHMATCH value in the switch at :442-458. At 8.3.0 `case SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_OTHER:` has only a `/* fallthrough */ comment (:446-447) and shares the body of SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_NOT_FOUND / UNKNOWN / ERROR, which sets `keymatch = CURLKHMATCH_MISSING;` (:453); only the `default:` arm assigns CURLKHMATCH_MISMATCH (:455-457). SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_OTHER is what libssh returns when the host is known but its key type differs from the recorded one, so a host whose key was replaced with another key type is reported to the CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION callback as an unknown host rather than as a mismatch (:513-517). A trust-on-first-use callback that accepts CURLKHMATCH_MISSING (typically returning CURLKHSTAT_FINE or FINE_ADD_TO_FILE, :520-531) then accepts the untrusted server, defeating SSH host verification for SCP/SFTP transfers over the libssh backend (CWE-297). Without a callback the MISSING verdict is still rejected (:537-541), so the defect needs the callback, matching the advisory. The 8.21.0 fix 0b8dbbc63 ("libssh: map SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_OTHER to CURLKHMATCH_MISMATCH", 2026-05-25) adds `keymatch = CURLKHMATCH_MISMATCH; break;` to that case, so the callback sees the mismatch and the documented callback logic rejects it. The fix marker is absent from the frozen file, where the only MISMATCH assignment is the default arm.

title: Caddy creates and pools a connection for the wrong upstream when forward_auth and reverse_proxy run together
category_l2: the selected upstream is published through the mutable request vars map instead of a request-scoped immutable value, so a concurrent forward_auth handler overwrites the dial info between RoundTrip and dial; the proxy transport connects to the auth upstream, pools that connection and serves proxy requests from it
affected_range: < v2.11.5 (repository-scoped advisory GHSA-6365-7ppr-5r92, published 2026-07-10, severity medium, patched_versions v2.11.5); the frozen snapshot is exactly tag v2.11.4 (annotated tag object 8ec11a4b peels to e2eee6a7), the last affected release

admission_checks.notes: Anchor at the frozen SHA: reverseproxy.go:663-665 is the comment and :666 `caddyhttp.SetVar(r.Context(), dialInfoVarKey, dialInfo)` inside proxyLoopIteration (func at :603); the read side is GetDialInfo at hosts.go:299-302 (`caddyhttp.GetVar(ctx, dialInfoVarKey)`), used by the dial closure at httptransport.go:275-293. Fix ancestry: 1830809afe8c is an ancestor of tag v2.11.5 (commit 0a137e2f; compare v2.11.5...1830809a: ahead_by 0, behind_by 89) and is 30 commits after v2.11.4 (compare v2.11.4...1830809a: ahead_by 30, behind_by 0), so it is absent from the frozen tree; its diff deletes exactly the :663-666 block and adds `ctx := context.WithValue(req.Context(), dialInfoCtxKey, di)` in reverseProxy. Severity: the repository advisory publishes severity=medium with cvss.score/vector_string null and an empty cwe_ids list, so level is medium with no score/vector; CWE-362 is an analyst mapping for the shared-state race, not vendor-published.

static_review_summary: reverse_proxy records the upstream it selected in the request's variable map: proxyLoopIteration calls `caddyhttp.SetVar(r.Context(), dialInfoVarKey, dialInfo)` (modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/reverseproxy.go:663-666), with `dialInfoVarKey = "reverse_proxy.dial_info"` (hosts.go:332-334). The transport's dial closure then recovers the target through `GetDialInfo(ctx)` (hosts.go:299-302), which reads the same map with `caddyhttp.GetVar(ctx, dialInfoVarKey)`, and overwrites network/address with it before `dialer.DialContext` (httptransport.go:275-293). The variable map is shared request state, and a new connection is dialled lazily when the transport needs one, so in a handler chain that runs `forward_auth` and then `reverse_proxy` the auth handler's SetVar can land between the proxy's RoundTrip and its dial: the proxy transport then dials the auth upstream, and the resulting pooled connection is used for proxy requests, which arrive at the wrong backend (observed as spurious 404s) and can make a `forward_auth` check pass against an endpoint that returns 200. The 2.11.5 fix 1830809afe8c ("reverseproxy: save dial info in a context key instead of a variable key to avoid race conditions when forward_auth is used", #7859) deletes the SetVar call and instead attaches the DialInfo to an immutable private context key right before the roundtrip (`ctx := context.WithValue(req.Context(), dialInfoCtxKey, di)`, reverseproxy.go:1032-1042), and GetDialInfo reads `ctx.Value(dialInfoCtxKey)`; the mutable-var pre-image present at v2.11.4 is exactly what the fix removes.

title: lodash _.unset/_.omit prototype pollution via array-wrapped path segments skips the constructor guard
category_l2: baseUnset's guard only inspects string segments while castPath leaves array segments intact and baseGet/toKey stringify them, so [["constructor"],["prototype"],"x"] walks to a built-in prototype and deletes a property there (Object/Number/String.prototype), bypassing the CVE-2025-13465 string-only guard
affected_range: >= 4.17.23, < 4.18.1 for lodash, lodash-es and lodash-amd (repository advisory GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh rows; the standalone lodash.unset/lodash.omit packages are < 4.18.0); frozen package.json version 4.17.23 is the first affected version (the 8-char prefix of tag 4.17.23, annotated tag object fd6aaf94 peels to dec55b7a)

admission_checks.notes: Fix pre-image at the frozen SHA: baseUnset spans lodash.js:4371-4414; :4374 carries the CVE-2025-13465 guard comment, :4385-4390 skip non-string keys, :4398-4409 block only the literal `constructor` -> `prototype` pair for string segments, and :4412-4413 delete the resolved parent key; the fixed form (`var key = toKey(path[index]);` plus a terminal constructor/prototype rejection) is absent. Supporting helpers verified in the same file: castPath :4556-4561, parent :6678-6680, baseGet :3070-3080, toKey :6856-6862. Fix ancestry: fe8d32ed is an ancestor of tag 4.18.1 (compare 4.18.1...fe8d32e: ahead_by 0, behind_by 7) and is 6 commits ahead of the frozen 4.17.23 tag commit dec55b7a (compare 4.17.23...fe8d32e: ahead_by 6, behind_by 0), so it is absent from the frozen tree. Severity is the repository advisory CVSS 3.1 6.5 MEDIUM with CWE-1321.

static_review_summary: baseUnset (lodash.js:4371-4414) validates path segments in a loop that skips every non-string key: `var key = path[index]; if (typeof key !== 'string') { continue; }` (:4385-4390). castPath returns an array path unchanged (:4556-4561 `if (isArray(value)) return value;`), so a segment can itself be an array and is skipped by that guard; the terminal deletion then resolves the parent through parent()->baseGet (:6678-6680, :3070-3080), which stringifies each segment with toKey (:6856-6862, `var result = (value + '');`), and deletes `obj[toKey(last(path))]` (:4412-4413). A call such as `_.unset({}, [['constructor'], ['prototype'], 'toString'])` therefore passes the guard untouched, walks to Object.prototype via `constructor`/`prototype`, and deletes a built-in prototype member; the same array wrapping bypasses the `constructor`/`prototype` pair check at :4398-4409 and the primitive-root exception it allows. The pre-existing CVE-2025-13465 guard (GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg, shipped in 4.17.23) is string-only, which is exactly the gap; the array-wrapped form reaches Object.prototype, Number.prototype and String.prototype and deletes properties (no overwrite of behaviour). The 4.18.1 fix fe8d32ed ("fix: block prototype pollution in baseUnset via constructor/prototype traversal") normalizes every segment with `var key = toKey(path[index]);` and rejects constructor/prototype as non-terminal traversal keys unconditionally, dropping the string-only skip and the primitive-root exception.

title: vendored flight decoder re-decodes every duplicate `$ACTION_REF_` field, so a Server Action form costs quadratic work
category_l2: the reply decoder re-decodes an identical `$ACTION_REF_` prefix once per duplicate field and rescans the whole FormData for each `$K` reference, with no dedup and no bound-args limit, giving O(N^2) work per request
affected_range: >=13.0.0 <15.0.8, >=15.0.0 <15.6.0-canary.61, >=16.0.0 <16.1.5 (Next.js advisory GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf); upstream React GHSA-83fc-fqcc-2hmg fixed in 19.0.4/19.1.5/19.2.4; frozen v14.2.24 is inside the first row

admission_checks.notes: Frozen snapshot: tag v14.2.24 is annotated (object ba09179a) and peels to 756be15c4cfecb6fae1c69cae7cfaf336423b6cf, the commit in the cached tree. Vendored build: packages/next/src/compiled/react-server-dom-webpack/package.json:50-51 pins `react`/`react-dom` to `18.3.0-canary-178c267a4e-20241218`; the bundle header names react-server-dom-webpack-server.node.development.js. Anchor: `function decodeAction(body, serverManifest)` :3620, body.forEach at :3626, `if (key.startsWith('$ACTION_REF_'))` :3634, `var metaData = decodeBoundActionMetaData(body, serverManifest, formFieldPrefix);` :3636, `action = loadServerReference(...)` :3637, closing brace :3656 (decodeFormState starts :3657); `function decodeBoundActionMetaData(body, serverManifest, formFieldPrefix)` :3603-3618 calls `createResponse(serverManifest, formFieldPrefix, body)` and forces `refPromise.then(...)`. Supporting facts: `function bindArgs(fn, args)` :3577-3579 is `fn.bind.apply(fn, [null].concat(args))` with no length check; `case 'K'` in `parseModelString` :3412-3429 runs `backingFormData.forEach(...)` over every entry. Absence checks: grep of the frozen bundle finds no `seenActions`, no `MAX_BOUND_ARGS`, no `arraySizeLimit`, no `$$consumed`, no `cycleProtection`; the same greps over react-server-dom-webpack-server.node.production.js are empty. Reachability: action-handler.ts:568 `if (isMultipartAction)` leads to :574 `const action = await decodeAction(formData, serverModuleMap)` (with decodeReply at :572 and decodeFormState at :579); the streaming branch re-resolves the same three functions at :619-622 and calls decodeAction at :665 after noting "React doesn't yet publish a busboy version of decodeAction" (:655). Fix ancestry: 99b450109dfd ("Sync DoS mitigations for React Flight", commits react 19.0.0-rc-4cd8f914-20260126) is contained in tag v15.0.8 (compare 99b4501...v15.0.8: ahead 1, behind 0, the extra commit being the release commit 16eb2af3); upstream de58cca00cf0 sits between v19.0.3 and v19.0.4 in facebook/react. Severity: the Next advisory publishes CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) and CWE-770; both are recorded as published, no re-scoring. Caveat recorded honestly: the advisory lists no 14.x patch, so the row anchors the in-tree vendored decoder rather than a Next-authored fix diff for this branch.

static_review_summary: Server Action POSTs whose body is multipart/form-data reach handleAction, which passes the request FormData to `decodeAction(formData, serverModuleMap)` (packages/next/src/server/app-render/action-handler.ts:574) from the vendored `react-server-dom-webpack-builtin` build. At the frozen v14.2.24 that bundle is 18.3.0-canary-178c267a4e-20241218 (packages/next/src/compiled/react-server-dom-webpack/package.json:50-51). Its `decodeAction` (react-server-dom-webpack-server.node.development.js:3620-3656) iterates every form field and, for every key that starts with `$ACTION_REF_`, calls `decodeBoundActionMetaData(body, serverManifest, formFieldPrefix)` (:3603-3618) with no record of which prefixes have already been decoded: the 19.0.4 hardening adds exactly that (`const seenActions = new Set<string>()` with an early return), and the frozen build has neither the set nor the `MAX_BOUND_ARGS` cap in `bindArgs` (:3577-3579). Each call builds a fresh response over the whole request body, closes it and forces initialization, and `parseModelString` case 'K' (:3412-3429) walks `response._formData` in full to rebuild each FormData reference, so one decode costs O(number of form fields) and N repeated `$ACTION_REF_` keys cost O(N^2) JSON parses and form scans while the request is parsed. The attacker controls both the field count and the repeated key, so a single request can occupy the server with excessive CPU (CWE-770, "allocation of resources without limits or throttling"), matching the advisory's "excessive CPU usage, out-of-memory exceptions, or server crashes" impact. The production bundle carries the same logic (`$ACTION_REF_` handling at react-server-dom-webpack-server.node.production.js:3223, no seenActions/MAX_BOUND_ARGS/arraySizeLimit anywhere in the file). The 14.2 line has no patch: the Next advisory (GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf, published 2026-01-26) lists 15.0.8 and later as fixed and its vulnerable range `>=13.0.0 <15.0.8` contains v14.2.24. The fix that ships in 15.0.8 is 99b450109dfd "Sync DoS mitigations for React Flight", which re-pins react and react-dom to 19.0.0-rc-4cd8f914-20260126; upstream the hardening is React 19.0.4 commit de58cca00cf0, released as 19.0.4/19.1.5/19.2.4.

title: actix-http accepts Content-Length together with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and lets chunked framing win, enabling CL.TE request smuggling
category_l2: the Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked flags are parsed independently and chunked silently wins, so CL+TE requests are accepted instead of rejected
affected_range: actix-http < 3.12.1, first patched 3.12.1 (GHSA-xhj4-vrgc-hr34); the frozen http-v3.12.0 tree is actix-http 3.12.0

admission_checks.notes: Frozen: tag http-v3.12.0 is commit a7a26f1ee0adfeabb5ee85a6eb2a62cff601a70b ("chore(http): release v3.12.0 (#3939)"), the tree cached at a7a26f1ee0ad; `actix-http/Cargo.toml` line 3 reads `version = "3.12.0"`, and the advisory lists "versions up to and including 3.12.0" as affected with first patched version 3.12.1. Anchor: `impl MessageType for Request` `fn decode` :231-315; `let mut length = msg.set_headers(&src.split_to(len).freeze(), &headers[..h_len], ver)?;` :276. Root cause in `set_headers` :75-213: `header::CONTENT_LENGTH` arm :106-127 sets `content_length`, `header::TRANSFER_ENCODING` arm :135-150 sets `chunked`, and the length resolution at :197-212 tests `chunked` (:198-202) before `content_length` (:205-209) with no check that both are absent/agree. The only same-request guards are duplicate-header checks (`multiple Content-Length` :101-104, `multiple Transfer-Encoding not allowed` :130-133) and the HTTP/1.0 POST rule :278-282, none of which look at the CL/TE combination. Frozen test that encoded the old behaviour: `hrs_cl_and_te_http10` :1118-1134 with the comment "in HTTP/1.0 transfer encoding is simply ignored so it's fine to have both" and `parse_ready!(&mut buf)`. Fix: 3c056bd36128d41ba130a8704ef5d648de3f2870 ("Merge commit from fork") touches actix-http/CHANGES.md, actix-http/src/h1/codec.rs and actix-http/src/h1/decoder.rs; the decoder hunk is inserted right after the :276 `set_headers` call and rejects HTTP/1.0 Transfer-Encoding, a non-chunked Transfer-Encoding, and Transfer-Encoding combined with Content-Length (pre-image of the hunk - the `// convert headers` comment, the `set_headers` line, a blank line and the HTTP/1.0 POST comment - matches :275-279 verbatim). The fix is contained in tag http-v3.12.1 (compare http-v3.12.0...http-v3.12.1: ahead 57, behind 0, including 3c056bd361 and the release commit 0fb89457ed). Severity and CWE are taken from the advisory record as published: GitHub CVSS v4.0 6.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N), medium, CWE-444; the CVSS v3 metrics are empty in the record and are not reconstructed. Candidate provenance: adv3_61724d22cf10bab7 was dropped from candidates.jsonl by the migration and is restored here from the pre-migration dossier (repo_vuln_benchmark-data-only-snapshot-20261026), which recorded it as `pending_version` because the repository advisory carried no first patched version at discovery time; the published advisory now does.

static_review_summary: The HTTP/1.1 request parser records `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` independently and never treats their combination as an error. In `Request::decode` (actix-http/src/h1/decoder.rs:231-315) the header block is handed to `set_headers` at :276; `set_headers` (:75-213) stores `content_length` for every Content-Length (:106-127) and sets `chunked` for `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (:135-150), then resolves the payload length by testing `chunked` first (`if chunked { PayloadDecoder::chunked() }` at :198-202) and only afterwards `content_length` (:205-209). Nothing compares the two flags, so a request that carries both is accepted and decoded as chunked, exactly the ambiguity RFC 9112 section 6.3 requires a recipient to reject. The frozen tree documents this as intended behaviour in its own test: `hrs_cl_and_te_http10` (:1118-1134) comments "in HTTP/1.0 transfer encoding is simply ignored so it's fine to have both" and expects the request to parse. With a front-end intermediary that frames on Content-Length while forwarding the conflicting Transfer-Encoding, the backend consumes only up to the terminating chunk, and the bytes the intermediary still attributes to the first request are parsed as a second request on the reused connection: classic CL.TE smuggling (CWE-444), reachable by any unauthenticated network client. The fix 3c056bd361 (released in http-v3.12.1) inserts the missing cross-check into `Request::decode` immediately after the `set_headers` call: it rejects Transfer-Encoding on HTTP/1.0, rejects a Transfer-Encoding that is not chunked (including `identity`), and rejects any request that carries Content-Length while Transfer-Encoding is present; it also flips the `hrs_cl_and_te_http10` expectation and adds `hrs_cl_and_chunked_te_http11`, `hrs_identity_te_http11` and a codec-level test.
